plan:
single-invocation pallas_call (no grid); K/V caches viewed as (L, B, W, H*D) and aliased to the outputs
(input_output_aliases), so untouched slots are never rewritten by the kernel; new tokens go HBM->HBM by DMA.
per sequence b the live token range [0, num_new) maps to at most two contiguous slot segments (ring wrap);
each segment is split into power-of-two chunks (static sizes, dynamic offsets) that cover all L layers in one DMA.
slot-position table and validity mask computed in-kernel on a (B, W) int32 VMEM block; only reshapes and the
int32->bool cast stay outside. Speed: data movement is just the new tokens (plus the alias copy XLA makes).

Grid (B,), offsets passed by scalar prefetch. Caches reshaped to (B,S,H*D), kept in HBM (pl.ANY) and aliased to the outputs, so XLA makes one copy of each cache, about what the reference costs.
Each step loads new_k[b] as a (T, H*D) VMEM block and applies RoPE in f32 inside the kernel. Cos/sin come from iota, offset and theta. Rotate-half uses pltpu.roll plus a select, with the roll direction checked on a rolled column index.
The bf16 result goes to a VMEM scratch, then is DMA'd to k_out[b, off:off+T]. new_v[b] is DMA'd HBM to HBM into v_out[b, off:off+T]. Both DMAs are waited on in the same step.
Outside the kernel: only reshapes and astype. Only the 2*B*T*H*D new elements are written; there are no matmuls or accumulators.

Grid (B, S//T): one step per sequence and per T-row block of the cache. Blocks are (1,H,T,D) for both caches and both outputs; the new k/v blocks stay fixed for each b. Offsets go in through scalar prefetch.
Each step copies the cache block to the output. Only the one or two blocks that overlap [off, off+T) do RoPE in f32: cos/sin computed in-kernel at full width, rotate_half done as a 64-lane roll with the sine sign flipped on the first half.
The rotated K and the V tokens are rolled down by r = off % T rows. A mask (rows >= r in block off//T, rows < r in the next block) picks new tokens over old cache rows.
Memory traffic is about the same as XLA's cache copy. 128 steps of about 4MB each keep per-step overhead low. vmem limit raised to 64MB.
Nothing runs outside the kernel except casting the offsets to int32.

K1 grid (T/256,) sequential: router dot (bf16 in, f32 acc), softmax/argmax/gate, in-block cumsum via a lower-triangular one-hot matmul plus a per-expert count carried in VMEM scratch, giving position/keep/flat slot. It also writes `out` directly (x*scale[e]*gate, with scale picked by a one-hot matmul) and a 32-bit packed copy of x (two bf16 per word; bf16 rows don't DMA cleanly).
K2 grid (E,) sequential, block out (1,C,H): flat slot index scalar-prefetched to SMEM. Step 0 builds the slot->token inverse with a scalar SMEM loop. Each step DMA-gathers the packed rows for expert e+1 into a double-buffered VMEM (2,C,H/2) int32 scratch (missing slots are DMA'd from a zero row), waits once for expert e's rows, unpacks to bf16 and stores the block.
Outside: only reshapes. All accumulation in f32.

Pass 1 (pallas): grid (m/512, k/1024), quantizes x in 128-wide groups (amax, divide, clip, e4m3 rounding with bit operations) and writes the dequantized x as bf16.
Outside the kernels: only w_fp8.astype(bf16), which is exact, and w_scale.astype(f32).
Pass 2 (pallas): bf16 matmul, grid (m/1024, n/1792, k/1024), blocks x(1024,1024), w(1792,1024), with w_scale (56,56) in SMEM. Each step multiplies the 128x128 weight blocks by their scale into a bf16 VMEM scratch, then does an NT dot_general with f32 accumulation.
The f32 output block stays in VMEM across k: it is set to the residual at k==0 and accumulated in place, so no extra scratch or epilogue is needed. vmem_limit is 100 MiB.
Speed idea: the reference runs a HIGHEST-precision f32 matmul (6 bf16 passes); we run a single bf16 MXU pass with large tiles.

Grid (L//T,) with T=128 time steps per step. The grid axis is "arbitrary" because the recurrence state h is carried across steps in a VMEM scratch of shape (B, 2N).
Per step: load the x block (B, T, H) and do B matmuls in bf16 with f32 accumulation: x_b @ [B_re; B_im]^T gives (T, 2N), which is scaled by gamma and stored time-major into a (T*B, 2N) f32 scratch using strided stores.
Scan: a fori_loop over T, where each step is one contiguous (B, N) tile for re and one for im, holding all batches. The complex update h = lam*h + bu runs on the VPU, and h overwrites bu in place (with -h_im stored).
Output: strided-load each batch's h rows as (T, 2N), multiply in bf16 by [C_re, C_im]^T with f32 accumulation, add D*x, and write the (B, T, H) block.
lam, gamma, exp, cos and sin are computed inside the kernel from the (1, N) parameters. Outside the kernel there are only reshapes, concatenates, transposes and bf16 casts of the weights. vmem_limit is raised to 96 MiB.

Flatten x to a lane-dense (rows, 1024) slab, padding the flat array to a multiple of 1024 only if needed. Grid is cdiv(rows, 1024) over (1024, 1024) blocks, about 4 MiB f32 per block. Double-buffered input and output come to about 16 MiB, so vmem_limit is raised to 64 MiB. All math runs inside the kernel in f32. It computes x * sigmoid(x) as x * 0.5 * (tanh(0.5x) + 1), which needs one transcendental per element and keeps the kernel bound by HBM bandwidth. Only reshape, pad and slice happen outside the kernel. The grid axis is marked "parallel".

Reshape x (N,C,H,W) to (N,C,R,128) with R=H*W/128; this is layout only. If H*W is not a multiple of 128, it keeps the block as (H,W).
Grid=(C,), parallel: each step loads one whole channel, block (N,1,R,128) = 2 MiB f32. Input plus output, double-buffered, comes to about 8 MiB of VMEM.
In the kernel, everything is float32. Each channel's statistics are computed in VMEM in two passes, first the mean and then the centered variance, which is numerically stable. The kernel then writes (x-mean)*rsqrt(var+eps)*gamma+beta.
gamma and beta are passed whole into SMEM and read as scalars. The only work outside the kernel is the reshape.
Speed: x is read from HBM exactly once and the output written once (512 MiB total traffic). XLA's fused version usually reads x two or three times.

Grid (C,): one channel per step, block (N,1,HW/128,128) f32 (2 MiB in + 2 MiB out, double-buffered ~8 MiB).
Pass 1: fori_loop over row chunks (<=256 rows) accumulating sum and sum-of-squares into (8,128) f32 vreg accumulators — no materialized centered temp.
Pass 2: fused out = x*scale + shift per chunk, scale = gamma*rsqrt(var+eps), shift = beta - mean*scale.
Outside the kernel: only reshape of x and astype of gamma/beta (passed via SMEM).
Speed idea: one HBM read + one write; per-element VPU work cut to ~3 ops (stats) + ~2 ops (output) vs previous multi-pass with VMEM temporaries.

Reshape x to (N*C, H*W) (layout-only); each row is one instance.
Grid (cdiv(rows,8),) marked parallel; block (8, H*W) = 2 MiB f32 in + 2 MiB out, double-buffered 8 MiB; vmem_limit raised to 48 MiB for in-kernel temps.
In kernel, accumulating in f32: mean via lane-sum, centered values, variance from centered values (two-pass like the reference), multiply by rsqrt, cast on store.
Only the reshapes stay outside the kernel. The op is memory-bound, so speed comes from one HBM read and one write with large lane-dense blocks.

Grid over (n*c)/16 row blocks, block (16, H*W) f32 = 4 MiB, giving 64 steps and about 16 MiB double-buffered (48 MiB VMEM limit).
Inside the kernel, two passes over the VMEM block in 512-lane chunks: pass 1 sums the values and their squares (shifted by each row's first element) in float32; pass 2 writes (x-mean)*rsqrt(var+eps).
No full-block temporaries; per-row values are broadcast once outside the loops; loops are unrolled up to 8.
Only the reshape to (n*c, H*W) and back happens outside the kernel.

Reshape x (layout only) to (N, G, C/G, S, L), where L=128 and S=H*W/128 when H*W is a multiple of 128; otherwise L=H*W and S=1.
Grid (N, G), both axes parallel. Each step loads one whole (sample, group) block (1,1,C/G,S,L), which is 4 MiB f32 here, so x is read from HBM once and written once.
Inside the kernel there are three loops over channels: a sum for the mean, a sum of squared deviations for the variance (computed in f32), and a write of x*scale+shift. Scale is inv*gamma[c] and shift is beta[c]-mean*scale; gamma and beta come from SMEM.
Partial sums are kept as (8,128) f32 sublane-reduced vectors and fully reduced once per group. vmem_limit is raised to 64 MiB so the 4 MiB blocks can be double-buffered.
Outside the kernel: only reshape and astype.

Grid (n, G), one (sample, group) block per step: (1,1,C/G,HW/128,128) f32 in and out, double-buffered (~16 MiB, vmem limit 64 MiB).
Pass 1 gathers sum and sum of squares together over (T,128) row chunks (T up to 64), with each lane shifted by the group's first row so the variance stays precise; f32 (8,128) accumulators.
Pass 2 normalizes each channel with one multiply-add (scale = inv*gamma, shift = beta - mean*scale) over the same chunks; gamma and beta are read from SMEM.
Speed idea: two VMEM passes instead of three, with chunked and partly unrolled loops, so the compute hides under the HBM transfers.
Outside the kernel: only reshapes and the f32 cast of gamma/beta.

Grid (N, C//cb) with cb = largest divisor of C that is <= 8, both axes parallel. Input block (1,cb,H,W) and output block (1,cb,H-1,W-1), both full spatial dims, so nothing is padded in HBM.
Inside the kernel, a fori_loop runs over the channels. Each channel is one (H,W) f32 tile, and the max is separable. Along each axis, m2[j]=max(x[j-1],x[j]) and m4[j]=max(m2[j],m2[j+2]) give the 4-wide window x[j-1..j+2]. The shifts use pltpu.roll (XLU), and iota masks fill the padding/wrapped positions with -inf.
That costs 2 rolls, 2 selects and 2 maxes per axis. The result is sliced to (H-1,W-1) on store. All work is elementwise in f32; there is no matmul or accumulator.
Nothing runs outside the kernel. The speed idea is a single HBM read and write, with the shifts kept on the XLU and the VPU work kept small.

layout (N, H, Cin, W) (one transpose+pad+bf16 cast outside): W on lanes, channels on sublanes. grid (N, cdiv(Ho, 16));
per step a (1, 16, Cin, Wr) row block plus a (1, KH-1, Cin, Wr) halo block; rows are lane-concatenated, the kw shifts
come from pltpu.roll, and the KW taps stack into K=KW*Cin so each kh is one (Cout, KW*Cin) @ (KW*Cin, 16*Wr) bf16 MXU
matmul with f32 accumulation (5 matmuls of K=448 per block instead of 35 of K=64).
output rows stored as (N, Ho, Cout, Wo); only the final slice/transpose to NCHW is outside.

stride-1 transposed conv = full conv with the flipped kernel; outside (layout only): pad x by K-1, flatten each (Hp,Wp) plane
to lanes (padded to a 128 multiple) and cast bf16 -> (N, Cin, Dp*Lin); weight -> (K, Cout, K*K*Cin) bf16 via flip/transpose.
grid (N, Do); K input specs fetch planes d..d+K-1 (block (Cin, Lin)); per kd the K*K taps are lane-rolls of the f32 plane,
stacked to a (K*K*Cin, Lo) bf16 patch and contracted on the MXU: acc(Cout, Lo) f32 += W[kd] @ patch.
output (N, Cout, Do*Lo) in a wide (Ho, Wp) row layout; the valid (Ho, Wo) window is sliced out by reshape/slice outside.

ConvTranspose as a stride-1 correlation over x padded by (K-1-p): sub-pixel phases become extra output channels (s^d*Cout), so no zero-dilated input.
x is padded/flattened to (B, Cin, D*Hp*Wp) with pitches picked so few tap offsets differ mod 128; grid (B, G, nL) over lane chunks L, halo = 2nd BlockSpec.
in-kernel im2col: one pltpu.roll per distinct lane remainder, 128-aligned lane slices per tap, taps stacked on sublanes, bf16 MXU dots with f32 accumulation.
groups=4 map to the G grid axis (channel blocks of Cin/G in, 8*Cout/G out); phase interleave + slice are layout ops outside.

same sub-pixel-phase flat conv as before: grid (B, G, nl), per group M = s^3*Cout_g = 256 output rows, bf16 MXU, f32 acc.
change: all T taps go into ONE contraction chunk (K = T*Cin_g = 768 <= 1024) instead of 3 chunks of 256, so the
(256 x L) f32 accumulator is written once instead of read-modify-written per chunk, and the MXU sees a deep K.
VMEM budget raised (48 MiB est, limit up to 110 MiB) so the single-chunk patch fits at the same lane tile.

outside (layout only): pad x, de-interleave the stride phases (reshape/transpose), slice the K tap windows and stack them
on the channel axis -> xs (N, K*Cin, Lout) bf16; weight (K,Cin,Cout) -> (Cout, K*Cin) bf16 by transpose/reshape.
kernel: grid (N, cdiv(Lout, TL)) with TL=2048; out block (Cout, TL) = W (Cout, K*Cin) @ xs block (K*Cin, TL), f32 accumulate.
one MXU matmul per step with K*Cin=192 contraction; the ragged last lane block is masked by Pallas on store.

ConvTranspose1d = stride-1 dilated correlation over the zero-interleaved input (lax.pad interior = layout op), taps at offsets dil*k, flipped kernel.
grid (B, 1, nL) over lane chunks L of the output length, halo (>= dil*(K-1)) as a 2nd 128-lane BlockSpec on the same flat array.
in-kernel: one pltpu.roll per tap offset, 3 taps stacked on sublanes -> (96->128, L) bf16, one MXU dot vs (Cout, 128), f32 acc.
output is written directly in its final (B, Cout, Lout) layout (partial last block masked), so nothing runs after the kernel.

x NCHW -> zero-padded (N, Hp, Cin, Wp) (transpose/pad outside, Wp lane-padded to 128k); grid (N, cdiv(H',16)): 16-row block + 8-row
halo block ((KH-1)*dh rows). Per step the rows are lane-rolled by kw*dw once into a bf16 scratch (KW, 24, Cin, Wp).
per output row, for each kh the KW taps stack into (KW*Cin, Wp) patches; MXU matmul (Cout, KW*Cin) @ patches, f32 accumulation over kh.
rows go to a (16*Cout, Wp) f32 scratch; per output channel a strided sublane load (stride Cout) yields its (16, W') NCHW block.
outside only transpose/pad of x and reshape/transpose/bf16 cast of w; garbage lanes >= W' are never stored.

Sub-pixel (phase) decomposition: output row/col phases (rh, rw) of the stride each get a plain correlation over x
with the taps k*d = r + s*m; grid (N, cdiv(A, TA)), TA=8 phase rows per step, x as (N, H, Cin, W) bf16 (transposed and
zero-padded outside, layout only) with a small row-halo block. Per row and phase: stack the tap rows (lane shifts by
pltpu.roll + mask) on sublanes and do one MXU dot (Cout, T*Cin) @ (T*Cin, lanes) with f32 accumulation.
Kernel writes (N, A, sh, sw, Cout, B); the phase interleave + crop to (Ho, Wo) is a transpose/reshape/slice outside.

ConvTranspose as a stride-1 correlation over x padded by (K-1-p): sub-pixel phases become extra output channels (s^d*Cout), so no zero-dilated input.
x is padded/flattened to (B, Cin, D*Hp*Wp) with pitches picked so few tap offsets differ mod 128; grid (B, G, nL) over lane chunks L, halo = 2nd BlockSpec.
in-kernel im2col: one pltpu.roll per distinct lane remainder, 128-aligned lane slices per tap, taps stacked on sublanes, bf16 MXU dots with f32 accumulation.
epilogue fuses conv bias and ((y+bias)+y)*y+y per phase (both biases as a (Cout',2) block); phase interleave + slice outside.

same sub-pixel-phase flat conv: grid (B, G=1, nl), M = s^3*Cout = 512 output rows, bf16 MXU dot, f32 acc, fused epilogue.
change: taps forced into a single contraction chunk (K = 8*Cin = 256) and lane tile target doubled (32768 lanes,
48 MiB VMEM estimate) so there are half as many grid steps and halo re-reads per output byte.
bias/residual/multiply epilogue stays fused in the kernel; outside only the phase-interleave transpose + slice.

grid (N, D_in): one step makes output depth pair od = 2t, 2t+1 for all Cout as a (Cout, 2, Ho, Wo) block; rows of the MXU result are (co, oh8) = 8 output rows per channel, lanes are (g, ow) with g = group of 8 output rows.
outside, only layout ops: x cast to bf16, W-upsampled by zero-interleave (even/odd ow parities, plus the iw+1 shifted copy), 5 strided H windows per row group, arranged as a (K=512, 512) bf16 slab per (n, d); weights gathered by slice/pad/concat into 3 (Cout*8, 512) Toeplitz-in-H matrices (kd = 1, 2, 0).
per step 3 bf16 MXU matmuls (512x512x512, f32 acc): pd=0 uses slab t, pd=1 uses slabs t and t+1 (slab t carried in VMEM scratch, so each slab is read once).
fused epilogue in f32 (+conv_b, +bias, +orig, *orig, +orig), stored as aligned (Cout, 8, Wo) tiles; per-channel absmax kept in a resident (Cout*8,128) VMEM max accumulator and reduced on the last step.
speed: one HBM write of the output (the floor), conv done on the MXU without the zeros of the dilated input.

x NCHW -> (N, H, Cin, Wp) (transpose/pad outside). Grid (N,) parallel: one whole image per step (GroupNorm needs per-image stats).
rows lane-rolled by kw once into an f32 scratch (3, H, Cin, Wp); per output row 9 taps stack into (9*Cin, Wp) bf16 patches and one
MXU matmul (Cout, 9*Cin) @ patches (f32 acc); epilogue sigmoid((y + conv_b + bias) * scale) stored to a (H'*Cout, Wp) f32 scratch
while masked per-channel sums accumulate; group mean, then a second pass for the (two-pass) variance, all in f32 in-kernel.
final pass: per channel a strided sublane load (stride Cout) gives its (H', Wp) plane, normalized * gamma + beta into the NCHW block.

Grid (N,); x transposed outside to (N, D, Cin, H*W) (layout only), the whole per-n block in VMEM. Spatial (h, w) is
flattened on lanes; per output depth d: Z = sum_kd W_kd (KH*KW*Cout, Cin) @ x[d+kd] (bf16 MXU, f32 acc), then the
KH*KW tap slices of Z are lane-rolled by kh*W+kw and summed (wrap-around only reaches invalid h/w positions).
Running min over d in a fori_loop (f32), then +bias and softmax over channels (sublanes) in f32.
Rows are stored straight into the NCHW output block (Cout, Ho, Wo) from 128-aligned lane offsets (one extra roll for
odd rows), so nothing but the input transpose and weight reshape happens outside the kernel.

call 1 grid (cdiv(B,1024), N/2048, K/512): x f32 block (1024,512) split in-kernel into bf16 hi+lo, w cast to bf16 outside (astype), two MXU dots accumulated in float32 directly into the resident z output block (1024,2048).
at the last K step call 1 also writes per-row-block BatchNorm partials (block mean, centered M2) with rows >= B masked, so the ragged 16300 batch never needs padding.
call 2 grid (N/2048, cdiv(B,512)): combines the partials (Chan) once per column block into mean / a = scale*gamma*rsqrt(scale^2 var + eps), then out = (z-mean)*a + beta (fresh output buffer).
bias b cancels exactly under batch-mean subtraction; outside the kernels only w.astype(bf16) and reshapes of the (N,) vectors.
speed: compute-bound bf16 MXU matmul with 2 passes for f32-level accuracy, x read only twice, w (bf16) read 16 times, normalize is one memory-bound pass.

x NCHW -> (N, H, Cin, W) (transpose/pad outside); grid (N, cdiv(OH,8)): each step makes 16 conv rows from a 16-row block + 2-row halo block.
rows are lane-rolled by kw once into a bf16 scratch; per conv row the 9 taps stack into (9*Cin, Wp) patches, one MXU matmul
(Cout, 9*Cin) @ patches, f32 accumulation; epilogue tanh(y + b - s1) - s2, row pairs summed, lane pairs pooled + compacted by a
0/1 selection matmul (data split bf16 hi+lo, f32 acc), x0.25. Pooled rows go to a (8*Cout, 128) scratch, and per channel a strided
sublane load (stride Cout) turns them into (8, OW) row blocks of the NCHW output block (1, Cout, 8, OW). Outside: layout ops only.

Grid (G*N/2,), 2 images per step; x reshaped (layout only) to (G*N, Ci, H*W) so each image is a (64, 4096) f32 tile with spatial on lanes.
Conv as one MXU matmul: im2col by 9 lane rotations (pltpu.roll by ky*W+kx) stacked to (576, 4096) bf16, (Co, 576) bf16 weights, f32 accumulation; garbage only lands at h>=62 or w>=62, never read.
Bias, -0.5, tanh, -0.2 in f32; 2x2 avg-pool + column compaction as a second matmul: 31 aligned 128-lane chunks (two image rows each) stacked to (31*Co, 128) @ (128, 128) pooling matrix built from iota.
Output written as (N, Ho, Co, Wo) and transposed to NCHW outside (layout only); weights reshaped/transposed outside.
Speed: input read once in NCHW (no NHWC copy), conv at K=576 on the MXU, pooling stays in VMEM.

Grid (N, Do); x transposed outside to (N, D, Cin, H*W) (layout only), per-n block resident across the Do axis.
Per output depth: Z = sum_kd W_kd (KH*KW*Cout, Cin) @ x[d+kd] as f32 MXU dots at HIGHEST precision (the reference is
HIGHEST), then the KH*KW tap slices of Z are lane-rolled by kh*W+kw and summed (flat-HW trick, wrap hits only invalid lanes).
Fused epilogue in f32: +conv_b, *scale, tanh, *bias, sigmoid; rows stored straight into the NCDHW output block
(Cout, 1, Ho, Wo) from 128-aligned lane offsets, so the large output is written exactly once.

Grid (N/bn, K/bk) with bn=2048, bk=512 and full M=1024 rows per block, so W is read from HBM once and x is read N/bn=4 times.
Blocks: x (M,bk), w (bk,bn), b (1,bn); out (M,1) stays resident. Tiles are cast to bf16 in the kernel; matmul accumulates in an f32 (M,bn) VMEM scratch.
After the last K step of each N tile: add bias, update running max/sum in f32 (M,1) scratch (one-pass logsumexp over N).
After the last N tile: final logsumexp, LeakyReLU x2, exact GELU x2 written to the output in the kernel. Outside the kernel: only b.reshape(1,N).
VMEM limit raised to 96 MiB; both axes 'arbitrary' because the max/sum state carries across N tiles.

MaxPool(2) then MaxPool(3) (VALID, disjoint) = one 6^3 max window; grid (N, Pd=10), each step covers 6 output depths.
x in: 5 depth-plane blocks (1,1,Hp=33,Cin=32,Wr=128) bf16 (W dilated by lax.pad outside); weights (5,5,64,160) bf16; bias (64,1).
fori over 5 chunks of 6 H-rows (2 pool groups): per (depth, H phase) sum of (64,160)@(160,768) bf16 matmuls, f32 acc, running max; then max over 3 q-rows, 6-lane window via pltpu.roll, +b, sum over channels.
Out (N,10,10,1,128) f32 (window max at every lane); stride-6 lane slice + reshape outside (layout only). Conv volume never hits HBM.

grid (G, N) = one sample per step ("arbitrary"); outside, layout-only ops split W into 32-wide output chunks (+2 halo), giving
x2 (G, N, nW, D*H padded, 128) with lanes (ci, u) and a shared banded "Toeplitz" weight (KD*KH*128, Cout*32) built by pad/tile/reshape.
in-kernel im2col: 9 sublane-shifted (D'*H, 128) slices per chunk -> A; conv = A @ Wt on the MXU in bf16x3 (hi/lo split, f32 acc),
as one K-stacked dot [A_hi|A_lo] @ [W_hi;W_hi] plus A_hi @ W_lo, giving (D'*H rows, Cout*32) per chunk kept in VMEM.
fused epilogue in VMEM: +b, *m, masked two-pass instance-norm stats per channel, clamp, *m, max over channels (vreg max + lane
rolls), stored straight into the (D', H', W') output block; no float math outside the kernel.

grid (N,): one whole image per step, layout (N, H, Cin, W) (transpose outside), W on lanes. Conv in row chunks: rows
lane-concatenated, kw shifts via pltpu.roll, taps stacked to K=3*Cin, bf16 MXU matmul with f32 accumulation, +bias,
written to a (Cout, Ho*W) f32 VMEM scratch while masked per-channel sum / sum-of-squares accumulate in f32.
GroupNorm stats via an iota group-indicator matmul (exact 3-way bf16 split); fold gamma/beta/scale into y*a+c; 4x4 max
pool = max of 4 aligned row slices + 2 lane rolls, lane compaction by an exact selection matmul; clamp; store (N,PH,C,PW).
Outside: input/weight transposes and the final small transpose to NCHW. Speed: conv output never leaves VMEM.

sub-pixel ConvTranspose2d (k4, s2, p1, op1): output phase (ph, pw) of grid point (m, l) needs xpad[m+dh, l+dw], dh/dw in {0,1,2}; outside (layout only) x goes channels-last, zero-padded, and the 3 W-shifts (+1 zero slot) are packed on lanes -> (N, Hp, 80, 4*Ci=256) bf16.
grid (N, 9 blocks of 8 grid rows): main block (None, 8, 80, 256) + 8-row halo; the 3 H-shifts are leading-dim slices, lane-concatenated to a (640, 768) bf16 im2col and one MXU dot with a (768, 4*Co) block-structured weight gives all 4 phases, float32 accumulation.
fused epilogue per 128-lane phase group: + conv bias, channel softmax (lane max/exp/sum), + bias, * 2, sigmoid; stored to a phase-interleaved (N, 72, 2, 80, 2*Co) output.
outside only reshape to (N, 144, 160, Co), slice to 129x129 and transpose to NCHW; 4x fewer MXU flops than XLA's zero-dilated conv.

sub-pixel (phase) decomposition of the stride-2 ConvTranspose: one (TH*Mw16, 12*Ci)@(12*Ci, 4*Co) bf16 dot per block
with f32 acc, softmax over channels per phase, +bias, *2, sigmoid, all fused; grid (N, Mh/TH), TH = divisor of Mh.
vs previous: the halo used to re-read a full TH-row block (2x input HBM traffic); now two 1-row halo BlockSpecs.
TH chosen to divide Mh (65 -> 13) so no padded output rows are computed/written (was 72 rows, 11% waste).

x is reshaped (layout only) to (N, C, R=HW/128, 128). Grid (N, C/Cb, R/Rb) with x blocks (1, Cb, Rb, 128), about 4 MiB per block (8 MiB double-buffered). For the bf16 config, Rb=512 and Cb=32, so the grid is (8, 4, 1).
Max pool: take the elementwise bf16 max over the Rb axis into an f32 (Cb,128) scratch. On the last r step, reduce over lanes to get a (Cb,1) column.
Linear layer: multiply the w block (Cb,O) in f32 by the column, then sum over sublanes into a (1,O) f32 accumulator scratch. This is exact f32 math on the VPU and costs little, because the kernel is limited by HBM bandwidth.
On the last channel block, add the bias and store to an output of shape (N,1,O); outside the kernel this is reshaped to (N,O). Outside the kernel there are only reshapes.
Speed: x (128 MiB) is streamed once in large blocks, with N parallel across cores.

x reshaped (layout only) to (N, C, R16, 16, 128), padded with -inf if H*W is not a multiple of 2048; grid (N, C/cb, R16/rb), block (1, cb, rb, 16, 128) of about 4 MiB.
Inside the kernel, a fori_loop over channels takes an elementwise max over the leading axis, so each step is one VPU max per bf16 vreg with no reduction across sublanes. The (cb, 16, 128) bf16 running max lives in VMEM scratch.
At the last row step: reduce across lanes to (cb, 1) in f32, multiply-and-sum with the w block, accumulate in a (1, O) f32 scratch, and add the bias on the last channel step.
Outside the kernel there are only reshape and pad; the bias is reshaped to (1, O).

x reshaped (layout only) to (N, C, H*W); lane tile t = largest multiple of 128 dividing H*W with a C*t*4-byte block of at most 2 MiB.
Pass 1 uses grid (N, HW/t), with every axis marked arbitrary. Each step reads a (1, C, t) block and adds 128-lane chunks into two f32 (C,128) VMEM accumulators for sum and sum of squares. These are plain VPU adds; the lane reduce runs once, at the last step. That step writes scale (C,1), shift (C,1) and logdet (1,1).
Pass 2 uses the same grid and blocks and computes out = x*scale + shift, so the scale and shift blocks stay resident.
HBM traffic is 2 reads + 1 write of x. Outside the kernels there are only reshapes.

Flatten x to (B*C, H*W); grid (cdiv(rows,256), cdiv(cols,2048)), blocks (256, 2048) f32 = 2 MiB, about 8 MiB double-buffered in+out.
gamma/beta reshaped and broadcast to a (B*C, 1) column outside the kernel (layout ops only); block (256, 1) per row tile.
Kernel does g*x+b elementwise in f32 and casts on store; no accumulator needed.
The kernel is memory-bound: one read and one write of x. Large lane-dense blocks and both grid axes parallel.
Not compiled, run or timed yet.

Grid (n, c//cb), both axes parallel. x is reshaped to (n, c, h*w) and each block is (1, cb, h*w) with cb=32 (1 MiB bf16, about 2 MiB as f32).
All math is in float32 and cast to the output dtype only on store.
Linear layer inside the kernel: the wT rows for gamma/beta (cb, sd) are multiplied by the style row (1, sd) and summed along the lanes, giving (cb,1) columns that broadcast over h*w.
Instance norm is one pass per block: mean, centred variance, then one scale-and-shift that writes the output.
Outside the kernel: only reshapes and one transpose (fc_w to (2c, sd), fc_b to (2c,1), s to (n,1,sd)). Memory-bound single pass: read x once, write the output once.

Grid (C/cb, N) with cb=32: x/out blocks (1, 32, H, W) bf16 = 1 MiB on the native 4D array; weight rows (32, sd) stay resident across N.
Per step: gamma/beta for 32 channels by a VPU multiply + lane reduce (f32) into (cb,1) scratch.
fori_loop over channels: each (H, W) tile in f32, two-pass mean/var, fused (1+gamma)*rsqrt scale and beta, cast to bf16.
Outside only layout ops on the tiny style/weight/bias (reshape, transpose); no reshape of x, so no relayout copies.

Reshape NCHW to (B*C, H*W), a free layout op. Grid is (rows/tr, cols/tc) with tr=256 and tc=8192, so each bf16 block is 4 MiB, or 8 MiB double-buffered. The row axis is parallel and the column axis is an arbitrary reduction.
Inside the kernel, each 128-lane chunk is cast to f32 and added into a (tr,128) f32 VMEM accumulator. This is VPU-only work. One cross-lane sum runs on the last column step, then the result is scaled by 1/(H*W) and cast to bf16.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes: (B*C,1) back to (B,C,1,1). The kernel is HBM-bound, and the large blocks keep per-step overhead low.

Reshape x (B,C,H,W) -> (N=B*C, S/128, 128) (layout only; fallback (N,S) if S%128!=0).
Grid (N//rb,) parallel; block (rb, S/128, 128) ~<=4 MiB (rb=16 here -> 4 MiB, 8 MiB double-buffered); output block (rb,1).
Kernel: upcast to f32, sum over axis 1 (cheap VPU adds), then a lane reduce with keepdims, multiply by 1/S, cast on store.
Memory-bound: one streaming pass over 268 MB with large blocks and a parallel axis for megacore.
Outside: only reshapes (input to 3D, output (N,1) -> (B,C,1,1)).

x (B,C,H,W) is reshaped outside the kernel to (N=B*C, L=H*W/128, 128). This is a layout op only. The grid runs over row blocks of rb rows, each up to 8 MiB, with "parallel" semantics.
Inside each block, an outer fori_loop takes 8 rows at a time. An inner fori_loop (unrolled) adds (8,8,128) slices into a float32 accumulator of 8 vregs that stays in registers. This avoids loading a whole 4 MiB block as one value, which spilled.
At the end, each group does one sublane reduction and one lane reduction, multiplies by 1/(H*W) and stores 8 rows of the (N,1) output. The only work outside the kernel is the final reshape to (B,C,1,1).
The kernel is memory-bound. Large blocks plus streaming accumulation should reach close to HBM bandwidth.

Flatten NCHW to (N*C, H*W) rows; this is a free reshape. Outside the kernel, broadcast weight and bias to (N, C) and reshape them to (N*C, 1); these are layout ops on small arrays.
Grid is (rows/bm, cols/bl), and both axes are marked "parallel". The default blocks are bm=8 and bl, the largest multiple of 128 that divides H*W and keeps the block at about 2 MiB of f32 (8x65536 at the default size).
Kernel: o = x * w + b, computed in f32 with lane-broadcast scale and shift, then cast on store. Per-step VMEM is about 8 MiB (input and output, each double-buffered).
Speed: the op is purely bandwidth-bound and reads and writes each element once with large lane-dense blocks, so it should match XLA's fused elementwise op.

View NCHW x as a lane-dense (N*C, H*W) slab. The grid is (rows/bm, hw/bn) with blocks of about (64, 16384) bf16, roughly 2 MiB each. Input plus output, double-buffered, comes to about 8 MiB of VMEM.
weight and bias are broadcast outside the kernel to (N*C, 1) columns. That is a layout op on 1024 elements. Each block uses a (bm, 1) slice of each column.
The kernel computes x*w+b in f32 and casts to bf16 on store. Nothing is accumulated.
Outside the kernel there are only reshape and broadcast_to. Both grid axes are parallel. The op is memory-bound, so the large lane-dense blocks should get close to HBM bandwidth.

Reshape x (N,C,H,W) -> (N,C,H*W) and weight (1,C,1,1) -> (C,1), both layout-only. Grid (N, C//bc, HW//bw); x/out blocks (None, bc, bw), weight block (bc,1) indexed by the channel-block axis.
bc = C (or a multiple-of-8 divisor of C), bw = the largest multiple-of-128 divisor of H*W that keeps a tile <= ~2 MiB (128x4096 f32). In plus out, double-buffered, is ~8 MiB of VMEM.
The kernel does o = x * w, broadcasting w along lanes, with arithmetic in float32 and a cast on store. No accumulator is needed.
Outside the kernel: only reshapes. All grid axes are parallel. The op is purely memory-bound, so wide lane-dense tiles stream at HBM bandwidth.

Flatten x to (N*C, H*W); grid (rows//bm, hw//bw) with blocks of about 4 MiB (here (16, 65536) f32, 64 steps) to cut per-step overhead on this memory-bound op.
The weight is broadcast to (N*C, 1) outside the kernel (layout only, tiny) and kept in VMEM for the whole call as one full block. Each step slices its bm rows.
Multiply is done in f32 in-kernel, cast on store; the VMEM limit is raised to 48 MiB for the 16 MiB of double-buffered in and out blocks.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes and the broadcast.

Flatten to (rows, 1024) bf16 lanes (pad if needed, layout only); grid over rows in (1024, 1024) blocks (2 MiB each, ~8 MiB double-buffered in+out), parallel semantics.
In-kernel: upcast to f32, sigmoid via 0.5*tanh(0.5x)+0.5, add 1, clip to [1.01, 2], cast back to bf16 on store.
Outside the kernel: only pad/reshape/slice. The op reads and writes memory without much compute (64 MiB in, 64 MiB out), so big lane-dense blocks keep HBM streaming at full rate.

Grid (rows/1024,), blocks (1024, 1024) bf16 = 2 MiB each, about 8 MiB double-buffered for input plus output.
Elementwise in bf16 (v6e VPU/EUP are bf16-native), so no widening to f32 and back.
Math: max(1.5 + 0.5*tanh(x/2), 1.01). One EUP op. The 2.0 max clamp is dropped because 1 + sigmoid(x) <= 2.
Outside the kernel: only reshape/pad/slice. The input size is already a multiple of 16384, so no pad.
Speed idea: the op is memory-bound, so cutting VPU work (no f32 casts, fewer ops) keeps it at HBM roofline.

Grid (B, HW/tk): batch axis is "parallel", reduction axis is "arbitrary". x is reshaped outside to (B, C, H*W); input block is (1, C, tk) bf16 with tk <= 8192 (about 2 MiB, 4 MiB double-buffered).
Each step sums its tk slice in 128-lane chunks into a local f32 (C,128) value, then adds it to an f32 VMEM scratch accumulator; no lane reduction until the end.
Last step: lane-reduce to (C,1), multiply by 1/HW, then (C,1)*w in f32 summed over C gives (1,nc); add bias and store the (1,1,nc) output block.
Outside the kernel: only reshapes of x, b and the output. The op is HBM-bound, so the kernel reads x exactly once in large contiguous blocks.

Grid (B, HW/tk); x reshaped to (B, C, HW), block (1, C, tk) bf16 with tk up to 8192, so a block is at most 2 MiB.
Spatial sum on the MXU: dot(x_blk (C,tk) bf16, ones (tk,128) bf16) adds into an f32 (C,128) scratch. The ones matrix is a broadcast built outside the kernel, and its block index never changes.
This takes the bf16→f32 casts and adds off the vector unit, which was the bottleneck, so the kernel should run at HBM bandwidth.
On the last k step: pooled = acc[:,0:1]/HW, then an f32 matvec on the vector unit against w (C,nc), plus the bias, and the result is stored as bf16.
Outside the kernel: only reshapes and the ones broadcast. VMEM is about 8 MiB and the limit is raised to 32 MiB.

Activations stay channels-last in a folded layout (N, H, W/f, f*C). Level 1 uses f=4, level 2 f=2 and level 3 f=1, so the folded width is 128 at every level and every lane count is 128 or 256. Each conv layer is one pallas_call with grid (batch, H/TH), where TH is 4 to 32 rows. Each source gets a main row block plus one-row top and bottom halo BlockSpecs.
Inside the kernel, three dots per row offset (bf16 in, f32 accumulate) cover the center quad. Two more dots handle the left and right neighbor pixels, and their f32 results are shifted with pltpu.roll and masked at the image edges. Bias and ReLU are added after the accumulation and the result is cast to bf16 on store.
Fused into the convs: conv1 runs as an in-kernel matmul on the im2col of x, ahead of conv2. The 2x2 maxpool is a second output of the convs that feed it. Bilinear 2x upsample and the skip concat happen inside the decoder convs, and the final 1x1 conv is fused into the last conv.
Outside the kernels: the NCHW->NHWC transpose, pad, slice and concat for conv1's im2col, and weight folding (slice, concat, zero blocks, pad, tile). The output reshape/transpose and the cast to bf16 are also outside.
Speed idea: folding pixels into lanes fills 256 MXU columns even when Cout is 64. Fusing pool, upsample and concat avoids writing those intermediate tensors to HBM.

Grid (B, HWp//hwb): x is reshaped to (B, C, HWp) and zero-padded to a multiple of 128 lanes if needed. Each step reads a bf16 x block of (1, C, hwb), at most 4 MiB, so 8 MiB with double buffering. B is marked parallel and the HW axis arbitrary.
Pooling adds 128-lane slices into a (C,128) f32 VMEM accumulator using only VPU adds. There is one cross-lane reduce per batch row, in the final HW step.
Final step, all in f32: pooled (C,1) times w1 (C,hid) gives h (1,hid) through a sublane reduce, then add b1 and ReLU. h is broadcast to (8,hid) and multiplied on the MXU by w2 zero-padded to (hid,128). Then come b2 and the Gumbel noise, lane masking, softmax, first-index argmax, the one-hot, and hard - soft + soft.
Outside the kernel: only reshape, pad and astype on the weights and noise, plus a slice and a bf16 cast of the (B,1,128) output.
Speed: the kernel is memory-bound and reads x from HBM exactly once in large lane-dense blocks.

Grid (B, HW/hwb): x is reshaped to (B, C, HW) and read in (1, C, hwb) bf16 blocks of up to 4 MiB, with the HW axis as the reduction.
The previous kernel was slow because the VPU had to convert and add every element (bf16 unpack plus f32 add). Now the pooling sum is one MXU matmul per step: x_block (C,hwb) @ ones (hwb,128), accumulated in f32 into a (C,128) VMEM scratch. bf16 inputs times exact ones give an exact sum, so the kernel stays bound by HBM bandwidth.
At the last HW step the same kernel does the rest: mean, FC1+ReLU on the VPU (f32), FC2 on the MXU at HIGHEST precision, then the masked softmax / argmax / one-hot gate. The output is padded to 128 lanes.
Outside the kernel there are only reshape, pad, astype and the final slice.

two pallas_calls over x viewed as (N, C, HW); blocks (1, C, T), T = largest 128-multiple divisor of HW with a <= 2 MiB block (8192 here); grid (N, HW/T).
call 1 accumulates per-(n, c) sum and sum of squares in float32 into (1, C, 1) output blocks resident across the HW axis.
call 2, at the first HW step of each n, turns those into batch mean/var, y = per-(n, c) mean, sigmoid(y @ fc_w + fc_b) and the gamma/beta mixtures (f32, VPU) -> VMEM scratch scale/shift (C, 1).
then every step streams out = x * scale + shift in f32 and stores bf16; outside only reshapes of x/out/fc_b and transposes of gamma/beta.
speed: x is read twice and written once (192 MB of HBM traffic), the minimum for batch stats; the tiny MLP runs once per sample.

No grid: x and out stay in HBM (pl.ANY). first_token comes in as a full (1,1,D) VMEM block.
In the kernel, broadcast first_token into a (1,B,D) VMEM scratch and DMA it to out[0].
out[1:] = x[:-1] is done as up to 8 concurrent HBM->HBM DMAs over seq-axis chunks, so nothing goes through VMEM and there is no per-step grid overhead.
No arithmetic and no accumulator, since this is a pure copy. The only thing outside the kernel is astype on first_token.
Speed idea: the copy is memory bound, so chunked DMAs should run near HBM bandwidth like XLA's own concat.

Grid (A, B/bb), with bb=16. The x block is (1, bb, D, C) in bf16, 2 MiB per block (4 MiB double-buffered). The mask block is the full (1, B, C), cast to f32 outside the kernel, which is a dtype-only change.
The f32 output block (1, D, C) stays resident across the B reduction axis and is used directly as the accumulator.
Inside each step, a fori_loop walks D in 32-row chunks. For each chunk it sums the bb masked items in registers, then adds the result into the output once.
On the last B step the kernel counts mask==1 over B, clamps the count to at least 1 and divides in place. Nothing is computed outside the kernel; only the mask astype happens there.
The work is memory-bound: one streaming pass over the 128 MB of x. The A axis is marked parallel.

view x/target (B,C,H,W) as (B,C,H*W); grid (B, HW/blk) both "arbitrary", blocks (1,C,blk) with blk up to 4096 lanes.
per step walk 128-lane chunks: one exp(-|x|) feeds both log1p (BCE) and sigmoid; accumulate p*t, p*p, t*t, bce
into four float32 (C,128) VMEM scratch accumulators (lane-wise partial sums, no cross-lane work in the hot loop).
last grid step reduces lanes -> per-channel dice, means, alpha*bce + beta*(1-dice) written to a (1,1) output.
outside the kernel only reshapes; single HBM pass over both inputs (memory bound), 1 exp + 1 log + 1 div per element.

was 0.44x XLA (VALU-bound): exact divide + log1p per element and four (C,128) carries (64 vregs) that spilled.
now per element: e=exp(-x), p=approx reciprocal(1+e) (2 EUP ops, no Newton/divide), s=max(p,1-p)=sigmoid(|x|);
softplus(-|x|)=-log(s) is summed as -log(prod s) over 32 chunks, so log runs once per 32 vregs instead of per element.
dice denom uses sum((p+t)^2) - 2*sum(p*t) (one accumulator fewer); ~14 VALU ops per element vreg.
fori_loop over 8-channel row groups (aligned sublane offset), static unroll over 256-lane chunks with 1-2 vreg
register accumulators; blocks (1,C,8192)=4 MiB per input, grid (B,HW/8192)=32 steps, all "arbitrary"; outside: reshapes.

Free reshape of the NCHW bf16 inputs to (B*C*H, W) = (131072, 256); grid over row blocks of (4096, 256) (2 MiB per input).
Each step runs a fori_loop over (16, 256) sub-tiles so the sigmoid / two logs / focal weights stay in vregs, all in f32.
Accumulator: (16, 256) f32 VMEM scratch; on the last step it is reduced to (1, 1) and scaled by loss_weight / divisor.
Outside: only the reshapes and the scalar reshape/astype.
Speed: single HBM read of both inputs, sigmoid as one tanh, (1-pt)**2 as a multiply.

Flatten both inputs to (rows, 1024); grid over row blocks of 256 (1 MiB per f32 input block), sequential ("arbitrary").
Accumulator: (8, 1024) f32 VMEM scratch, summed by folding row groups (pure VPU adds); final cross-lane sum and /N at the last step.
Outside the kernel: only reshape to 2D and reshape of the (1,1) result to a scalar.
Speed idea: single HBM pass over both inputs, sigmoid/log on the EUP, no intermediate arrays.

Flatten both inputs to (rows, 1024) via reshape; 1-D grid over row blocks of 512 rows (2 MiB f32 per input block, about 8 MiB double-buffered), marked "arbitrary".
Inside each block, a fori_loop over 32-row slices keeps an (8, 1024) f32 running sum in registers, which is added to a VMEM accumulator once per block.
Speed: the math is rewritten to use 2 transcendentals per element instead of 4: log_p = -log(1+exp(-x)), log_1mp = log_p - x, with the -100 clamp on both terms.
The final step writes -sum/n into a (1,1) output. Outside the kernel there are only reshapes and an astype.

Grid (B, H/16): batch parallel, row blocks arbitrary; x block (1, C, 16, W) f32 read in its native NCHW layout (no
(C, H*W) relayout copy); the (C, C) f32 gram accumulator lives in VMEM scratch across the row blocks.
Pixels can be summed in any order, so per image row r the block gives X_r = (C, W) by a stride-16 sublane gather and
gram += X_r X_r^T as a bf16 NT matmul with f32 accumulation (values feed a sqrt and a global L2 norm; error << 1e-2 tol).
Last row block: scale by 1/HW, signed sqrt, global sum of squares, normalize, write the (1, C, C) block.
Outside: only the final (B, C, C) -> (B, C*C) reshape. Speed: one read of x; MXU work ~34 GFLOP vs the HIGHEST reference.

Elementwise, memory-bound. Reshape all 4 inputs to a lane-dense 2D slab (N/L, L), with L=1024 when divisible, else the last dim.
Grid = cdiv(rows, 256), block (256, L) f32 = 1 MiB per array; 5 arrays x 2 buffers ~ 10 MiB VMEM. Dimension marked parallel.
All arithmetic is f32 inside the kernel: divide, round with the same STE expression as the reference, clip to [-(q_p-1)*is_signed, q_p], multiply by delta.
Outside the kernel: only reshapes. The -1 offset comes from symmetric=False in the reference config.

Grid (N,): one image (1, 1, H, W) float32 per step, everything stays in VMEM; outputs (1, 4, 10, 127, 127) float32.
Conv1 and conv2 (+bias, relu) run on the VPU in float32 over 64-row chunks (dy via sublane rolls, dx via lane rolls,
weights as SMEM scalars); 2x2 pooling = stride-2 row loads + lane-pair max into a full-map scratch, then the
even-column decimation of the whole stage is one one-hot MXU matmul (bf16 hi/lo split stacked on M, ~2^-17 exact).
torch's view(-1, 4) on NCHW: each pair of pooled rows (2*254 = 4*127 values) is spread by one more one-hot matmul
into 4 lane blocks (element 4q+k -> block k, lane q) for all 4 channels at once; Linear(4,8)+relu, Linear(8,10) and
softmax are float32 VPU math on (127, 127) planes. Outside: one transpose/reshape into the (N*64516, 10) row order.
Speed: a single pass over the 128 MiB input; no 4- or 8-wide intermediate ever lands in HBM.

Kernel 1 (conv+bias+ReLU): grid (B, cdiv(Ho,256)). Each step loads a 256xW block of x plus an 8-row halo block (index clamped at the edge). The 3x3 windows come from pltpu.roll on the sublane and lane axes. Conv weights and bias are SMEM scalars, the math is f32 on the VPU, and the output is written as (B,C,Ho,Wo) with Wo set to the full array dim.
Outside the kernels, layout ops only: flatten, pad to a multiple of 128 and reshape to (R,128). Each row then holds 16 groups of 8, because Wo%8!=0 means the rows of 8 do not line up with image rows. fc_w is tiled to (128,64) and fc_b to (1,64).
Kernel 2 (linear+bias+ReLU): grid cdiv(R,4096), blocks (4096,128) -> (4096,64). An iota mask inside the kernel makes the tiled weight block-diagonal, the matmul is f32 at HIGHEST precision with an f32 accumulator, then bias and ReLU.
Afterwards, the (R,64) output is reshaped to (R*16,4) and sliced to M rows. Both kernels are memory-bound; aligned rolls avoid unaligned relayouts, and the 128-wide rows keep lanes full.

Flatten pred/gt to a lane-dense 2D layout (R, L) with L=1024 when the total size allows, otherwise L=width. Grid runs over row blocks of up to 512 rows (multiple of 16 for bf16) and is sequential ("arbitrary").
Pass 1 (pallas_call): diff = where(gt>eps, |pred-gt|, 0) in f32. It keeps a running elementwise max in an (8, L) f32 VMEM scratch and writes 0.5*max as a (1,1) f32 output on the last step.
Pass 2 (pallas_call): reads the (1,1) threshold, computes the loss in f32 and accumulates the loss sum and valid count in (8, L) f32 scratch. On the last step it writes sum/count as (1,1) f32.
Outside the kernels: only reshape and the final astype to the input dtype. Each pass is one memory-bound sweep that reads both inputs once, the same pass count as XLA.

Two passes over the data; neither runs any float math outside the kernel. Inputs are flattened to (R, 1024) bf16, with up to 1024 rows per grid step.
1. Pass 1 computes the diff in native bf16, which halves the vector work and matches the reference's bf16 diff exactly. It keeps a running max in registers over 32-row chunks (fori_loop), folds that into an (8, L) f32 scratch, and outputs 0.5*max.
2. Pass 2 reads the threshold, rebuilds the bf16 diff per chunk, converts it to f32 and applies BerHu. It sums the loss and the valid count in f32 register values, then folds them into (8, L) scratch. The last step writes sum / count.
3. If the shape doesn't divide cleanly, it falls back to one block per step with full reductions. Only reshape and astype run outside the kernels.
Speed: larger blocks plus a register-resident chunk loop, so the kernel is limited by memory bandwidth rather than the VPU.

Flatten to (rows, 1024) lane-dense; grid over 512-row blocks (2 MiB f32 per block), "parallel".
Elementwise in f32: x * tanh(beta * log(1 + exp(x))); pow folded into a multiply since log(a^b) = b log a.
Outside: only reshape in and out. Speed idea: memory-bound single pass, wide lane-dense tiles, transcendental work on the EUP.

The input is flattened to (rows, 1024) and processed on a 1-D grid of (512, 1024) f32 blocks (2 MiB each, 8 MiB with input and output double-buffered). The axis is marked parallel.
Everything is computed in f32. The only work outside the kernel is two reshapes.
To make it faster, the old version's exp, log and tanh become one exp and one approximate reciprocal. With beta = 1.5, tanh(1.5*log(s)) = (s^3 - 1)/(s^3 + 1), where s = 1 + e^x.
The numerator is computed as t*(3 + 3t + t^2) with t = e^x, so very negative x loses no precision. x is clamped at 20 before the exp so s^3 cannot overflow.

Grid (B//512, N//8): batch tiles parallel, teacher chunks sequential; input_t block (512, 8, Dd), U block (8, H, H), output (512, N) resident.
Chunk 0 computes s = enc(input_s) (bf16 scratch) and seeds the f32 logits with s W_e^T + b.
Each chunk: t = dec(input_t block) as one (4096, Dd) x (Dd, H) matmul into scratch; per teacher a strided row read of t,
q = s U[n] + W_d[n], logit[:, n] += sum(q * t_n); the last chunk does the softmax over N in f32.
bf16 MXU operands, f32 accumulation. Outside: weight astype/bias reshapes only. Speed: one pass over input_t, t and s U never hit HBM.

Grid is (N/512,) over the flattened rows N = batch*dim1*dim2, marked parallel. Each step loads x1 and x2 blocks of (512,128) f32, already padded with the constant 1 outside the kernel by jnp.pad, then transposes them in the kernel to (128, tn).
The full weight is a resident (O, D1*D2) bf16 block (W.reshape, 4 MiB). An fori_loop over pairs of i builds P = [x1T[i]*x2T; x1T[i+1]*x2T] as (256, tn) bf16 and adds W[:, chunk] @ P into a VMEM accumulator of shape (O, tn) in f32. This is the bilinear form done as a matmul with K=256 and no lane reductions.
At the end the accumulator is transposed to (tn, O), the bias is added and the result is stored. Outside the kernel there are only reshape, pad (value 1.0) and astype to bf16 on the weight.
Speed: about 550 GFLOP on the bf16 MXU with no HBM intermediates, while XLA's lax.map makes HBM round trips for every output channel.

Flatten x to a lane-dense 2D slab (total/1024, 1024); if the size doesn't divide by 1024, use (prod(leading dims), last dim). The reshape is the only work outside the kernel.
Grid is cdiv(rows, 1024) over 1024-row blocks, marked parallel. Each bf16 block is 2 MiB, so input plus output, double-buffered, is about 8 MiB of VMEM.
Inside the kernel: upcast to f32, compute a stable logaddexp max(c,y)+log1p(exp(-|c-y|)) with y = margin - x, and cast back to bf16 on store.
Memory-bound, so one streaming pass in large blocks should be about as fast as XLA's fused elementwise op. margin=0.5 and const=1.0 are hardcoded because CONFIG can't be read; they are loss parameters, not sizes.

Flatten to (rows, 1024); grid over 512-row blocks (2 MiB f32), sequential ("arbitrary") because of the running sum.
Accumulator: (8, 1024) f32 VMEM scratch, row groups folded with VPU adds; one cross-lane sum, / N and * alpha at the last step.
Outside: reshape in, reshape the (1,1) result to a scalar.
Speed idea: single streaming pass, reciprocal and clamp fused, no intermediate array.

Flatten pred to (rows, 1024) via reshape; 1-D grid over row blocks of up to 1024 rows (4 MiB f32 tile, 8 MiB double-buffered, vmem limit raised to 48 MiB).
Inside each step, a fori_loop walks 32-row chunks and keeps an (8, 1024) f32 accumulator in registers, so the full 4 MiB intermediate is never written back to VMEM.
The reciprocal uses pl.reciprocal(approx=True), which runs on the EUP instead of a multi-op VPU divide. Its relative error (about 1e-4) is far inside the 1e-2 tolerance.
The (8, 1024) scratch carries the sum across grid steps. The last step does the final reduce and the alpha / N scale. Outside the kernel there are only reshapes and an astype.
Speed idea: the previous version was VALU-bound (divide plus a materialized intermediate). These changes should bring it close to HBM bandwidth with fewer, larger grid steps.

Flatten x (layout only) to a lane-dense 2D slab (M, L), L in {1024,512,256,128}; grid (M // TR,), TR rows ~4 MiB per block.
Each step loops over 32-row chunks: d = max(|x - 0.5|, 0.01) in f32, folded into an (8, L) f32 VMEM scratch accumulator with vreg adds.
The last step reduces the accumulator to a scalar and writes alpha / sum into a resident (1, 1) f32 output block.
Only reshapes stay outside the kernel; x is read from HBM exactly once (memory-bound, like XLA's single reduction fusion).

Flatten the input to a lane-dense (R, L) slab, L=512 when it divides evenly. Grid (R//bm,) with (bm, L) blocks of about 2 MiB bf16, double-buffered.
Inside the kernel, a fori_loop walks the block in chunks of about 32 f32 vregs into an (8, L) f32 carry, which is added to a resident (8, L) f32 VMEM scratch. The last grid step writes the mean to a (1,1) f32 output.
Math: |sigmoid(x)-0.5| = 0.5|tanh(x/2)|, so each element is 2/max(|tanh(x/2)|, 2*min_diff). That is one tanh plus one approximate reciprocal per element, keeping the kernel near the HBM bandwidth limit.
Outside the kernel: only a reshape of the input, and a reshape/astype of the scalar result.
Assumes center == 0.5 (tanh identity) and a total element count divisible by 1024.

Kernel 1 (pooling): x reshaped to (b, c, HW); grid (b, HW//tk), tk=8192 (a divisor of HW that is a multiple of 128; falls back to full HW). Block is (1, c, tk).
The f32 running sum and max are carried in (c,128) registers over 128-lane chunks with fori_loop, then saved to VMEM scratch between steps. At each batch's last HW step the lanes are reduced and the full gating chain runs in f32 on (c,1) columns (softmax, the three dot products, tanh), writing the gate (tanh(...)+1) as (1, c, 1).
Kernel 2 (rescale): same grid; x block (1, c, tk) times the gate block (1, c, 1) broadcast along lanes, cast on store.
Outside the kernels: only reshapes (x to (b, c, HW), biases to (c, 1), output back to NCHW).
Speed: 3 HBM passes of x, the same as XLA's reduce plus elementwise. vmem_limit is 64 MiB so the 4 MiB double-buffered blocks fit.

Outside (layout only): x -> stride-4 polyphase planes (N, 4, 4, 256, 256) bf16, so every conv tap and every 2x2/stride-2 pool
of both stages becomes one of 25 (layer 1) / 36 (layer 2) aligned planes shifted by 0 or 1 (pltpu.roll), built once per image in VMEM.
Kernel 1, grid over images: both conv2x2 + maxpool + relu stages on the VPU in f32 over 8-row strips (accumulators stay in vregs,
weights as SMEM scalars), layer-1 phases written straight into the layer-2 source planes; output (N, 8, 256, 256) bf16.
Outside: slice to 255x255, flatten in NCHW order (view(-1, 8)), pad rows to the block size (layout only).
Kernel 2: 16 groups of 8 share a 128-lane row, so Linear(8,32)+relu+Linear(32,4) run as lane-dense block-diagonal bf16
matmuls (128x512, 512x128) with f32 accumulation over (1024, 128) blocks; result reshaped to (-1, 4).

Grid over batch tiles of Bt=64 (32 steps, "parallel"); per step input block [H+4, Bt, W*Cin] (H-major, row-padded, lanes=(w,c)).
Each conv runs as a banded (Toeplitz) matmul: out_rows[h] = sum_kh in_rows[h+kh] @ T[kh], T: [k, Win*Cin, Wout*Cout]. Output columns are ordered (w parity, w/2, c), so the 2x2 max-pool is a max of two lane halves plus a max of adjacent leading rows. Bias and relu are applied after pooling, which gives the same result because both commute with max.
Matmuls take bf16 inputs and accumulate in f32 over chunks of 8 output rows (M=512). Pooled bf16 activations go to VMEM scratches with zeroed padding rows. fc1/fc2/fc3 run in the same kernel and write a (Bt, 7) block.
Outside the kernel there are only layout ops: input transpose/reshape/pad; Toeplitz weights built with pad, static slices, stack, transpose and reshape; fc1 rows permuted from NCHW-flatten order to (h, w*c); biases tiled/reshaped.
Weights (~13 MB) stay resident because their block index is constant; vmem_limit is raised to 100 MiB.

Pass 1: grid (B,) over feature_t transposed to (B,P,C) with block (1,P,C). It sums over positions into a (1,C) f32 output block that stays resident, then divides by B*P to get the channel mean.
Pass 2: grid (B, P/tp) with tp=256, both axes sequential. At j==0 the kernel centers and L2-normalizes target block (P,C) and stores it in VMEM as bf16 hi/lo halves. Each step normalizes the input tile (C,tp), then three bf16 matmuls (hi*hi + hi*lo + lo*hi) give dist (P,tp) in f32 at near-f32 precision.
The per-element work is folded into one formula, w = exp(min(alpha[p] + beta[p]*d, b/sigma)). It reads the column min from the max of dist over target positions. A column sum gives the softmax, and a running elementwise max goes into a (P,128) VMEM scratch.
At the last tile of each sample the kernel reduces max -> mean -> -log into a (1,1) scratch accumulator. At the very last step it writes the mean over the batch to the (1,1) output.
Outside the kernels: reshapes, the (B,C,P)->(B,P,C) transpose and the final astype. vmem_limit is raised to 100 MiB.

x (N, 4) viewed lane-dense as (N/64, 256): 64 tokens per row; output (N/64, 128) is exactly the row-major (N, 2) result. Grid over 2048-row tiles, "arbitrary" (selectors built at step 0).
r and phi are de-interleaved onto the output lanes by two exact bf16 one-hot matmuls (256 x 128) on the otherwise idle MXU, f32 results.
out = r * sin(phi + pi/2 on even lanes), so one sin per element gives both cos and sin; cast to bf16 on store.
Outside: reshapes only. Speed idea: no strided channel slices or stack, all loads/stores full-lane.

Grid (N/8,) over the merged leading dims. The input (B*D1, D2, 4) is read in blocks of (8, D2, 4) and the output (B*D1, D2, 2) is written in blocks of (8, D2, 2), both in the original tiled HBM layout. That avoids the relayout copies that probably caused the 0.10x result.
Inside the kernel a fori_loop works through 128-row pieces in float32. r is the slice of channel 0. phi is a masked sum across the 4 channels, which avoids an unaligned lane shift.
Each output pair is r * sin(phi + [pi/2, 0]), so there is one transcendental per element instead of a cos and a sin.
Outside the kernel there are only free reshapes of the leading dims. The VMEM limit is set to 48 MiB because each padded block takes about 2 MiB. None of this has been run yet, so the speed and the Mosaic lowering are unchecked.

no grid (single invocation); x and out stay in HBM (memory_space=pl.ANY), no VMEM blocks.
per batch b, two HBM->HBM DMAs: x[b] -> out[b, :C] and x[b, :S] -> out[b, C:C+S] (S = out_C - C).
all 2*B DMAs are started first, then waited, so many copies are in flight and HBM stays saturated.
no arithmetic at all (pure copy, dtype preserved); nothing outside the kernel; speed = one read + one write of the data.

x as (B, C, H*W); grid (B, HW/4096), block (1, 64, 4096) f32 = 1 MiB, "parallel"; output (B, 2, HW) with block (1, 2, 4096).
Max and mean over the channel (sublane) axis in f32, written as rows 0 and 1 of the output block (the concat).
Outside: reshapes only. Speed idea: one read of x, both reductions from the same VMEM tile, concat written in place.

x as (B, C, D*H*W); two pallas_calls over grid (B, S/4096) with blocks (1, 128, 4096) bf16 = 1 MiB (the gate needs the full spatial mean first).
Pass 1 (batch "parallel", spatial "arbitrary"): f32 (C, 128) scratch of lane-chunk sums; at the last spatial step the mean, both tiny FC layers (VPU broadcast-multiply + reduce, f32) and the sigmoid produce a (C, 1) gate per batch.
Pass 2 ("parallel"): x * gate, f32 multiply, cast to bf16.
Outside: reshapes and a transpose of w2 (layout). Speed idea: two streaming passes, the minimum; the squeeze/excite MLP costs nothing.

grid=(B,) marked "arbitrary". x and out stay in HBM (pl.ANY). Each batch slab (C, S) bf16 is copied into a VMEM buffer with two slots (2*C*S*2 B = 32 MiB, so vmem_limit_bytes is raised), in 8 lane chunks of (C, 8192).
Mean: an f32 (C,128) running sum while chunks arrive. The two FC layers, ReLU and sigmoid run on the VPU in f32 at each step.
Scale: bf16 multiply in place in VMEM, then copy each chunk back to HBM as soon as it is done. The load of batch b+1 into the other slot starts after the sum for batch b, so it overlaps the scale and write-back of batch b.
Outside the kernel: reshape x to (B,C,S), transpose w2 and reshape the biases. HBM traffic is 1 read plus 1 write of x, against XLA's 2 reads plus 1 write.

Inputs are reshaped to a lane-dense 2-D slab (R, L). L is 1024 when the element count allows it, otherwise the original width. Grid is (R//tb,), marked "arbitrary". Each step reads one (tb, L) block of x and y with tb up to about 1024 rows (2 MiB per bf16 block, about 8 MiB double-buffered).
Inside the kernel a fori_loop walks 32-row chunks: upcast to f32, compute sqrt(d*d+eps), and fold it into an (8, L) f32 accumulator kept in VMEM scratch.
On the last step the kernel reduces the accumulator, divides by the element count and writes an (8,128) output tile.
Outside the kernel there is only the reshape, a [0,0] slice and an astype back to the input dtype.
Speed: each input is read from HBM once, in large blocks, with only vector-unit work.

Inputs are reshaped to (R, 1024) lane-dense 2D arrays. The 1D grid runs over row blocks of up to 4 MiB of bf16 each; at full size that is about 2048 rows per step and 16 steps. Two inputs with double buffering use about 16 MiB, so vmem_limit is raised to 48 MiB.
Inside each step, a fori_loop (unroll 8) walks 32-row chunks. The subtraction is done in bf16 to halve VPU work, then cast to f32 before square + eps + sqrt. Results are summed into an (8, L) f32 carry, which is added to a VMEM scratch accumulator.
On the last step the kernel reduces the scratch to a scalar, multiplies by 1/n, and writes an (8,128) output block. Outside the kernel there are only reshapes, the [0,0] slice and astype.
Speed idea: bigger blocks mean fewer grid steps, and the bf16 diff plus deeper unrolling keeps the VPU work hidden under HBM bandwidth.

Flatten x,y (layout-only reshape) to (R, W) with W=1024 if total%1024==0 else the last dim; grid=(R//bm,) with bm chosen so each input block is about 2 MiB (multiple of 8 dividing R, else full R).
Kernel: read both tiles, cast to f32, compute sqrt((y-x)^2+eps), fold into an (8,W) f32 VMEM scratch accumulator via reshape(bm//8,8,W).sum(0), using vector adds only.
On the last grid step: reduce the accumulator to a scalar, multiply by 1/N, and write a (1,1) output. Outside the kernel only reshape that output to ().
Speed: one streaming HBM pass over both inputs (memory-bound), large blocks double-buffered (about 8 MiB total VMEM), no extra passes.

Flatten x and y (a layout-only reshape) to a lane-dense 2-D array of shape (R, L), using L=512 (or 1024/256/128, or the last dim if none of those divide the total size).
The grid is 1-D over row blocks of up to 2048 rows. Each bf16 block is 2 MiB, so 2 inputs x 2 buffers is about 8 MiB of VMEM. The axis is "arbitrary" because one accumulator stays live across all steps.
Inside the kernel, a fori_loop walks 64-row chunks: upcast to f32, compute sqrt(d*d+eps), and fold the chunk into an (8, L) f32 scratch accumulator with VPU adds only.
On the last step, the kernel reduces the accumulator to (1,1) and casts it to the output dtype. Outside the kernel there is only a reshape to a scalar.
The task is memory bound: the kernel reads 128 MB once at HBM speed, which should match XLA's fused reduce.

Flatten all three inputs to a lane-dense (rows, 1024) slab. If the element count isn't a multiple of 1024*8, pad with jnp.pad and slice off the padding afterwards (layout ops only).
Grid is cdiv(rows, 512) with (512, 1024) f32 blocks, about 2 MiB each. Three inputs plus one output, double-buffered, comes to about 16 MiB, so vmem_limit_bytes is raised to 64 MiB.
The kernel computes maximum(minimum(x, max), min) in the input dtype. There are no matmuls, so no accumulator is needed.
Outside the kernel there are only reshape, pad and slice. The axis is marked parallel. Speed comes from large blocks that stream HBM at roofline in a single fused pass.

Grid (B*C/32,); input block (32, H*W) f32 = 2 MiB, output block (32, 1).
Max and sum over the lane axis in f32, mean = sum / (H*W), add, store.
Outside the kernel: reshape to (B*C, H*W) and back to (B, C, 1, 1).
Speed: memory bound single read of x; parallel axis splits rows across both TensorCores.

Grid (N, H/16), both parallel; blocks (1, C, 16, W) f32 in the native NCHW layout (no transpose, no relayout copy).
In VMEM the block is viewed as (C*16, W) rows (c, h); image row h for all channels is a stride-16 sublane gather
(strided vld), 4 rows are lane-concatenated into a (C, 4W) channel-major tile, and both 1x1 convs are W^T @ tile on the
MXU (bf16 in, f32 acc) with bias + LeakyReLU fused; results go back with strided stores into the output block.
Outside: weight reshape/transpose/bf16 cast and bias column reshapes only.
Speed: one read and one write of 256 MiB (memory bound); both convs and activations fused, 34 GFLOP on the MXU.

One pallas_call, grid (2 phases, rows/32) over arrays viewed as (B*C, H*W); blocks (32, H*W) f32.
Phase 0 streams current/original and accumulates squared diffs into an (8, H*W) f32 VMEM scratch (vector adds only).
Phase 1 reduces the scratch to a scalar once, then streams weight and writes weight * total; index maps park unused inputs so they are not refetched.
Outside the kernel: reshapes only.
Speed: memory bound, minimal traffic (read cur, orig, weight once, write output once), no second launch.

Grid (B*C/64,) over inputs viewed as (B*C, H*W) bf16; blocks (64, H*W), output (1, 1) f32.
Loss computed in f32 per element, folded into an (8, H*W) f32 VMEM accumulator with vector adds; final cross-lane sum and the 1/(2*batch) scale on the last step.
Outside the kernel: reshapes and the final f32 -> bf16 cast of the scalar.
Speed: one streaming read of both inputs, 2 MiB blocks, no intermediate HBM arrays.

Flatten both bf16 inputs to (R, 1024) as a layout op. Pad with zeros only when the size is not a multiple of the block; zeros give zero loss. Grid over row blocks of (1024, 1024) bf16, 2 MiB per input per step, double-buffered, with the reduction axis marked arbitrary.
Inside each step, a fori_loop (unrolled 8x) goes over (16, 1024) chunks. The loss is computed in bf16 (packed 16x128 vregs, matching the reference's bf16 elementwise math), cast to f32, folded down to (8, 1024), and added to a register carry. The full f32 loss tile is never stored to VMEM.
The carry is added into an (8, 1024) f32 VMEM scratch each step. On the last step it is fully reduced and scaled by 1/(2*bs) into a (1, 1) f32 output.
Outside the kernel: reshape, pad, the final reshape to a scalar, and astype to bf16.

Grid (batch, H/64); bf16 NCHW blocks (C, 64, W=256) plus 16-row halo blocks above/below (clamped index maps, zeroed at the edges).
Rows are re-laid as a row-major (row, channel) bf16 scratch with the SAME pad (1 top, 2 bottom): the bf16 block is viewed as u32
row pairs, sublane-strided loads (stride H/2) fetch a row pair for all channels, shifts/masks split it into two exact rows.
Per output row one MXU matmul Wbig (4Co [kw], 4Ci [kh]) @ (4Ci, 256) with f32 acc; kw taps are lane rolls with edge masks (pad 1/2),
+ bias, rounded to bf16 bits and two rows packed per u32 word for the strided store back to NCHW.
Outside: weight transpose/reshape/cast only. Speed: no NHWC transposes in HBM, x read 1.5x and written once, MXU-bound.

Grid (B, H/32); x main block (1, Cin, 32, W) float32 plus 8-row halo blocks above/below, all in native NCHW;
output block (1, Cout, 32, W) float32 written NCHW, so no transpose touches HBM.
Rows are gathered as (Cin, W) matrices with sublane-strided loads into a bf16 (35, Cin, W) scratch (TF SAME pad 1/2
handled by zeroed halo rows). Per output row one MXU matmul: wmat (4*Cout, 4*Cin) [dx,co | dy,ci] @ 4 stacked rows
(512 x W), float32 accumulation; the 4 dx partials are lane-rolled with edge masks and summed, bias added in float32.
Speed: K=512, M=512, N=256 per matmul (~275 GFLOP total) with ~1.3x input read; output via strided stores.

Grid (N, ceil(Ho/8)); whole padded NHWC bf16 image per batch element resident, weights (k*k, C, O) bf16 resident, output block (1, 8, Wc=144, O) f32.
16 taps paired along K: 8 matmuls of (8*144, 2C) @ (2C, O) per step into an f32 accumulator; bias and PReLU (shared slope) in-kernel.
Outside the kernel: NCHW->NHWC transpose, zero pad, bf16 casts, weight transpose; slice off the alignment padding and transpose back.
Speed: one bf16 MXU pass (XLA default precision), K = 256 fills the v6e MXU, image fetched once per batch element.

Single fused pallas_call, grid=(batch,) parallel, one image per step: x block (1,3,512,512) bf16, cast once to an f32 VMEM scratch.
Conv1: for each 64-wide block of pooled columns, the 15 row-shifted (508,256) input slices are concatenated per input channel and multiplied by a banded weight matrix (1280,768) with f32 accumulation. The 768 output columns are ordered (width parity, channel, j), so width pooling is a max of two 384-lane halves; height pooling uses stride-2 row reads from scratch. Then bias + relu, and the result goes to an f32 VMEM scratch p1 (254,1536).
Conv2: same idea on p1 (K=3840, N=1024, blocks of 32 pooled columns), followed by pooling, bias, relu and a bf16 store into an output of shape (N,125,2048).
Outside the kernel: only pad/broadcast/reshape/slice/transpose to build the banded weight matrices and bias rows (skew trick), plus the final transpose, slice and flatten.
All weight matrices stay resident in VMEM (memory_space=VMEM, about 21 MB); vmem limit raised to 100 MiB.

Grid (B, H*W/4096); edges block (1, C, 4096) f32, weight row block (1, C, 1), output block (1, 1, 4096).
Softmax of the weight row over C in-kernel (f32, recomputed per step: 128 values), then a sublane-axis weighted sum in f32 on the VPU.
Outside the kernel: reshapes only.
Speed: memory bound single read of edges, lane-dense output.

Grid (B//128,) over images, x read in native NCHW blocks (128, 3, 32, 32); every stage stays in VMEM, output (128, 10).
conv1 as width-Toeplitz matmuls: channels packed on lanes by one-hot MXU placements, kernel rows paired so K = 256, N = (co, ow) padded to 256;
row shifts by kh are unaligned sublane reads from an f32 scratch. ReLU, then 2x2 max-pool as lane roll + max and stride-2 row reads.
conv2 the same on pooled lanes (one matmul per kernel row), pool, then fc1 as 5 matmuls on stride-8 row reads, fc2, fc3; bf16 MXU, f32 accumulation.
Outside: only layout ops on the small weights (banded Toeplitz via concat/broadcast/slice/reshape, permutes, zero pads) and astype.

One pallas_call per ConvTranspose2d, NHWC, grid (batch, output phase-row blocks of 16); blocks (1, 16, Wphys, Cin) plus a 2-row "previous block" halo spec on the same input.
Stride-2 layers use the sub-pixel decomposition: per output row phase, sum over (a, b) tap offsets of (16*Wq, Cin) @ (Cin, 2*Cout) bf16 MXU matmuls, f32 accumulate; the two column phases share lanes so the output (n, m, py, w, (px, c)) reshapes for free to (n, 2m, 2w, c).
Zero padding/halo, input row masking and out-of-range output zeroing happen in-kernel; intermediates are bf16 with zeroed tails so no pad/crop between layers.
Outside: NCHW<->NHWC transposes, weight regrouping (pad/reshape/transpose/astype), bias concat, final crop.
Speed: no lhs-dilated input is ever built (XLA convolves 75% zeros), bf16 MXU instead of the reference's HIGHEST f32.

Four pallas_calls. conv1: x is reshaped for free to (N,C,H/4,4W). Grid (N, H1s/32), with a 16-row halo block. Inside the kernel, rows go into an f32 scratch, (128 x W) slabs are transposed on the XLU, and stride-4 sublane loads split out the W phase. That builds an LHS of shape (288, 1152) with lanes (dw,c,u,row) plus a halo block. It is multiplied by a pre-arranged block-Toeplitz weight of shape (1152, 256), giving lane-dense output (N, 36, 288, 8 rows x 32 ch).
conv2 (stride 2, 4x4) and conv3 (3x3) work on that layout. Rows of the image sit in lanes, so the H-direction taps are a Toeplitz in the weight. W-direction taps are stride-2 or shifted sublane loads from an f32 scratch, and the next chunk serves as the halo. Both use grid (N, 36/4), bf16 MXU inputs and f32 accumulation, with bias and ReLU fused.
FC: a tiled matmul (800 x 1568) @ (1568 x 512) with f32 accumulation, plus bias and ReLU.
Outside the kernels: only reshape, transpose, pad, stack, slice and broadcast, used to build the weight matrices and tile the biases, and for the final NCHW flatten of the small conv3 output.

Reshape each sample to (B, Rp, 128) lanes. If needed, pad with p=0, t=0; padding adds nothing to any sum, and the BCE term is 0 because log(1)=0 and t=0.
Grid (B, Rp/TR) with TR=2048 rows, so each block is (1, 2048, 128) f32 = 1 MiB. Two inputs, double-buffered, use about 4 MiB of VMEM. Both grid axes are sequential.
Inside each block, a fori_loop over 256-row chunks keeps four (8,128) f32 accumulators: p*t, p, t and the BCE term l1 + t*(lp - l1). Each log is clamped at -100. The four sums go into VMEM scratch.
At the last row block of each sample, the kernel reduces the sums to (1,1) and adds that sample's Dice coefficient to a dice accumulator. At the last grid step it writes -bce_sum/N + 1 - dice/B to a (1,1) output.
Outside the kernel there is only reshape, pad and the final reshape to a scalar. The kernel reads its input once and has no float temporaries in HBM, so speed is limited by memory bandwidth.

Reshape both inputs to (N, C, HW/128, 128) as a layout op only. Grid is (N, HW/(128*R)), blocks are (1, C, R, 128), and R is picked so each block is about 2 MiB of f32.
All arithmetic is in the kernel: sigmoid, p*t, p+t. Two f32 VMEM scratch accumulators of shape (C, 8, 128) are updated by folding R into R/8 x 8 and summing over the leading axis, which is mostly plain vreg adds.
On the last grid step the kernel reduces the accumulators to per-channel sums, computes dice with the epsilon clamp, and writes the mean to a (1,1) f32 output.
Outside the kernel there is only reshape plus a final reshape/astype to a scalar. Each input is read once from HBM, so the kernel is memory-bandwidth bound; both grid axes are 'arbitrary' because the accumulators are shared across steps.

flatten each sample (layout reshape) to (B, R, L) with L=1024 lanes; grid (B, R//tm), block (1, tm, L) ~2 MiB per input.
three float32 (8, L) VMEM accumulators (sum p*t, sum p, sum t) updated with pure VPU adds per step.
at the last row-chunk of a sample reduce to (1,1), form the dice coefficient, add it to a (1,1) running total.
at the very last grid step write 1 - total/B into a resident (1,1) output; only reshapes stay outside the kernel.
speed: one streaming pass over both inputs (HBM-bound), no intermediate arrays.

Flatten both bf16 inputs to a lane-dense (rows, 512) slab and zero-pad to a whole number of blocks. Zero padding adds nothing to the sum: |0-0|/0.6 = 0.
Grid (rows/2048,) with "arbitrary" semantics. Each input block is (2048, 512) bf16 = 2 MiB, so double-buffered inputs use 8 MiB of VMEM.
Inside each step, a fori_loop walks 64-row chunks, upcasts them to f32 and computes the SMAPE terms with exact division. Each chunk is folded into an (8, 512) f32 loop carry, which is added to a VMEM scratch accumulator.
On the last step the kernel reduces the accumulator to a scalar, casts it to the input dtype and writes a (1, 1) output. Outside the kernel there is only reshape, pad and a final reshape to ().

Grid (batch, n_nodes/2048): h_pl and h_mi blocks (1, 2048, n_h) bf16, c row (1, 1, n_h), W (n_h, n_h) resident; output block (1, 2, 2048) of (B, 2, N), reshaped for free to the (B, 2N) concat.
Reassociated bilinear: v = W c computed in-kernel per step (bf16 MXU, f32 acc), then scores = h . v as a lane-dense NT matmul v2(8, n_h) . h^T with v split into bf16 hi/lo rows.
f32 accumulation throughout; bias added in f32, cast on store.
Outside: reshapes and bias astype only.
Speed: O(N*n_h) instead of O(N*n_h^2) work, so the kernel is purely bandwidth bound on the 128 MiB of h.

Grid (batch, num_nodes/2048): h_pl and h_mi blocks (1, 2048, n_h) bf16, c slice (1, 2048), W (n_h, n_h) resident; output block (1, 2, 2048) of (B, 2, N), reshaped for free to the (B, 2N) concat.
Because c_x broadcasts c[n] along n_h, the bilinear collapses to c[n] * (h . u) with u = W summed over its last axis (computed in-kernel by an NT ones-matmul, f32 acc).
Scores via a lane-dense NT matmul of u split into bf16 hi/lo rows against h; times c, plus bias, f32.
Outside: reshapes and bias astype only.
Speed: bandwidth bound on h (128 MiB) instead of an O(N*n_h^2) einsum.

Grid (B, C/8); input block (1, 8, H, W) f32; output viewed as (B, 2, C, H/2, W/2) with block (1, 2, 8, H/2, W/2), so both concat halves come from one read.
Rows: stride-2 sublane load. Columns: one-hot (W, W/2) selector built from iota, f32 split hi/mid/lo bf16 -> three MXU dots, exact copy.
Second half written as y * 0 in-kernel (keeps NaN/inf propagation). Outside only the final reshape.
Speed: x read once, output written once, no concat or strided-slice copies in XLA.

Grid (B, ratio, C/TC) over the input reshaped (free) to (B, C, H*W); blocks (1, TC, H*W) of at most 2 MiB (TC=16 for bf16 here).
Kernel divides by s*s in the input dtype (exact for s=1); ratio copies > 0 write y*0 to keep NaN/Inf semantics.
No accumulator needed; outside only reshapes.
Speed idea: one lane-dense streaming copy, large blocks to sit at HBM bandwidth.

No grid: one pallas_call with input and output left in HBM (memory_space=pl.ANY).
With STRIDE == 1 and RATIO == 1 the reference is an exact identity (x/1, with NaN and Inf preserved), so the kernel only copies.
It starts B HBM-to-HBM DMAs (one per batch element, each with its own DMA semaphore) all at once, then waits on all of them.
Nothing passes through VMEM and there is no vector compute or accumulator. The old version was slow because of the bf16 divide.
Nothing runs outside the kernel. If STRIDE or RATIO changes, an assert stops the run.

Grid (B, HW/2048) over inputs viewed as (B, C, H*W); blocks (1, C, 2048) bf16, output (B, 1, H*W) with block (1, 1, 2048).
In f32: difference, square, sum over the channel (sublane) axis; stored as bf16.
Outside only reshapes. Speed: one read of both inputs, output is C times smaller; parallel grid.

Four pallas_calls of one fused matmul + bias + ELU kernel, bf16 MXU operands, f32 accumulate, bf16 activations between layers.
Layer 1: the five dilated stride-2 branches become one (pixels, 640) x (640, 40) block-diagonal matmul over a layout-only im2col (strided slices + concat); grid (B, 128/16).
Layers 2-4 (k4 s2 p1): pad + space-to-depth + two-column concat outside, so each conv is 2 row taps (leading-axis slices) of (Ho*Wo, 8C) x (8C, Cout); grid (B,), whole image per step.
The 2x2 avg pool is fused into the last layer: its columns are pre-ordered even/odd so the pair sum is two aligned halves. Weights single-buffered (pl.Buffered(1)), vmem limit 100 MiB.
Speed idea: every FLOP is on the MXU with K >= 320; no compute on padding beyond the 1-pixel border.

Grid (N, O//bo) with bo=32: x laid out (N, Hp, C, W) and resident per sample, w as (kh, kw, O, C), output tile (1, H', bo, W'), so O tiles along sublanes.
Both spatial shifts are handled per tap: H as a free leading-dim slice (H padded outside), W as a lane slice plus zero concat on f32 values, inside the kernel.
Matmuls take bf16-exact inputs and accumulate in float32 in a VMEM scratch (H', bo, W'), filled in 16-row chunks to limit register pressure.
Bias, per-channel instance norm over (H', W') and LeakyReLU are fused in the same step, since each step holds every spatial position for its channels; cast to bf16 on store.
Outside the kernel: only transpose, pad and reshape. vmem_limit_bytes is raised to 32 MiB for headroom (about 15 MiB estimated).
Speed idea: x is fetched once per sample and reused across channel tiles, so HBM traffic is near minimal. Not compiled or timed here.
