Grid (N,) "parallel", one image per step: x as (N, H+2, Ci, W) bf16 (H-padded transpose outside), weights as (kw*Co, kh*Ci) = (512, 512).
Per output row (fori over 127): one bf16 MXU matmul (512, 512) @ (512, W) with f32 accumulation; the kw tap groups are
shifted along lanes with pltpu.roll and masked at the W padding, summed into an f32 (Co, W) row stored in a VMEM scratch.
InstanceNorm stats in f32 (sum pass, centered-variance pass) from that scratch, then LeakyReLU and a bf16 store per row.
Outside: the NCHW -> (N, H, C, W) transpose + pad and the inverse output transpose (layout only); bias cancels in the norm.
Speed idea: 127 large matmuls per image instead of 2032 tiny f32 ones, no lane-concat copies, each image read once.

Stride = L/2, so each output step t uses frame t and frame t+1 of length-stride frames. Outside (layout only): pad T to whole 128-lane frame blocks, reshape/transpose x to frames (B, C*s, T/s) and w to (N, 2*C*s).
Grid (B, cdiv(Tout, 4096)) "parallel"; block (1, C*s, 4096) of frames plus a (1, C*s, 128) look-ahead block; pltpu.roll builds the t+1 frames.
One (N, 2Cs) x (2Cs, 4096) bf16 MXU matmul with f32 accumulation per tile (bf16 products are exact, matching HIGHEST), ReLU, store bf16 (1, N, 4096) with time on lanes.
Speed: the 537 MB bf16 output dominates; it is written once, lane-dense, and the input is read about once.

Grid (D0*D1/16,) over the input viewed as (D0*D1, 128, 512) (leading-dim merge only); bf16 block (16, 128, 512) = 2 MB.
A fori_loop over 32-row chunks: row max on the XLU, z = x - max, e = exp(z) in f32; e and e*z are folded to 128 lanes with vreg adds and the row sums finished on the MXU with a ones (128,128) bf16 matrix (f32 accumulate), giving S and T replicated across lanes.
Per row sum_j p log p = T/S - log S, accumulated in a (32,128) f32 carry / VMEM accumulator; the last step reduces and scales by -1/(D0*128).
Outside the kernel: leading-dim reshape, (1,1)->() reshape, astype to bf16.
Speed: one pass over 128 MB; log_softmax, exp and the product never reach HBM, and two of the three row reductions use the MXU instead of the XLU.

Grid (rows/TR,) over x reshaped (free) to (B*C, H*W); blocks (TR, H*W) of about 1 MiB (TR=32 rows of 16384 bf16 lanes).
Kernel upcasts to f32, computes 1/x + x^4 (a + x (b + c x)) with Horner, masks x >= 1 to zero, casts back to bf16 on store.
No accumulator; outside only reshapes.
Speed idea: pure elementwise stream at HBM bandwidth; one divide per element.

Flatten x to (N, 512) lanes. Grid over row blocks of up to 2 MiB bf16 (for example 2048x512), marked parallel, with the VMEM limit raised to 32 MiB.
Inside each block, fori_loop over 16-row chunks so the f32 temporaries stay in vregs instead of spilling large intermediates to VMEM.
The math runs in f32: 1/x via pl.reciprocal(approx=True) on the EUP (no VPU divide), x^4 via two squarings, Horner for a + b x + c x^2, then the where-select and a cast to bf16 on store.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes. A full-array single-block fallback handles odd sizes.

Reshape (B,C,H,W) to (B,C,HW); grid (B, HW//T) with T=4096 (1 MiB bf16 per input block, ~4 MiB double-buffered).
Inside the kernel: a static loop over 512-lane chunks; a fori_loop over 16-channel slices applies sigmoid as 0.5*tanh(0.5x)+0.5 in f32 and accumulates (8,512) f32 sums of p*t, p and t in registers.
After the channel loop: reduce over sublanes, compute per-pixel F-beta, add into a resident (1,512) f32 VMEM scratch.
Both grid axes are 'arbitrary' (global mean); the last step writes 1 - sum/(B*HW) to a (1,1) output. Outside the kernel there is only a reshape to a scalar.
Speed: each input is read from HBM once, so the kernel is bandwidth-bound; per-element work is one tanh plus a few FMAs.

Reshape pred/gt to (N, rows, 1024); grid (N, rows/512), (1, 512, 1024) f32 blocks, reduction axis last.
Per-sample f32 (8, 1024) VMEM accumulator, stable logaddexp(0,-p) = max(-p,0) + log(1+exp(-|p|)).
Last step per sample writes sum/count broadcast into a (1,1,128) output block; outside only reshape and slice [:,0,0].
Speed: one pass over both inputs, one exp and one log per element, memory bound.

Grid (B, H/32); x transposed outside to (B, H, C, W) so a row is a (C, W) tile; main block (1, 32, C, W) plus top/bottom 1-row halos (zeroed at the image edge) copied into a bf16 scratch.
Per output row: one bf16 MXU dot (3*mid, 3*C) @ (3*C, W) with f32 accumulation, dx taps combined by lane rolls + edge masks, bias added, then the 1x1 conv as a second dot (n_classes, mid) @ (mid, W).
Output written as (B, H, n_classes, W) and transposed back to NCHW outside; weights reshuffled/bf16-cast outside.
Speed idea: both convs fused, the 256-channel mid activation never touches HBM; K=384 / K=256 matmuls.

Grid (rows/TR,) over both inputs reshaped (free) to (B*C, H*W); blocks (16, 65536) bf16, about 2 MiB each.
Kernel upcasts to f32, computes |x-y|/c - log(1 + |x-y|/c), sublane-sums into a (1, H*W) f32 scratch.
Last step reduces the scratch, scales by c^2 and writes a (1,1) output; outside only reshapes and the bf16 cast of the scalar.
Speed idea: single streaming pass, one log per element, HBM bound.

Grid (B, HW//T) with T = r*W ≈ 1024 lanes (r whole image rows). The x block is (1, Cin, T) taken straight from x reshaped to (B, C, H*W), so x is never transposed.
Each step runs 5 matmuls Wt(cout,cin) @ h(cin,T) with bf16 operands and f32 accumulation. The f32 bias add, LeakyReLU and sigmoid happen in-kernel.
AvgPool(1,25) is a matmul s(1,T) @ P(T, r*Wo) at HIGHEST precision. P (block-diagonal, 1/25 entries) is built from iota into a VMEM scratch when j==0.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes, transposes of the weights to (cout, cin), and astype; the output is (B, nT, 1, r*Wo), reshaped to flat.
Speed: x is read once (memory-bound, ~2 MB per step, double-buffered), and all intermediates stay in VMEM.

Grid (B, H/8); x block (1, C, 8, W) f32 in native layout (2 MiB VMEM), weights bf16 and biases f32 as constant blocks.
Per step: 8 stride-8 sublane loads of the (C*8, W) ref view give each row's (C, W) slab; an NT matmul with a WxW identity
transposes it exactly into a (8*W, C) bf16 scratch; 4 bf16 matmuls (f32 acc, f32 bias + leaky relu) with M = 512 rows;
last layer as an NT matmul to a lane-dense (8, 512) row, f32 sigmoid, width-25 window sums by 6 lane rolls + adds.
Outside: weight reshape/astype, and a reshape + slice of the 512 KiB window-sum output down to (B*H*Wo,).
Speed idea: no relayout copy of x, MXU-sized matmuls with stationary weights, and no HIGHEST pooling matmul.

Reshape x (N,C,H,W) -> (N*C, H*W); grid over row blocks of br rows (multiple of 8 dividing N*C, ~2 MiB per block -> (32, 16384) f32 for the reference shape), full H*W on lanes.
Per-row params: scale/bias/threshold broadcast to (N,C) and concatenated to (N*C,3) outside (layout ops only); block (br,3).
In-kernel: f32 lane reduction mean(x^2), rsqrt, fold into per-row coef = s*rsqrt and offset = b-t, then y = max(x*coef + off, 0) + t; single pass, one read + one write of x.
VMEM: 2 MiB in + 2 MiB out, double-buffered = 8 MiB < 16 MiB. Grid axis 'parallel'. Memory-bound; matches XLA's fused roofline.

Inputs viewed as (B*C*H, W) rows (leading-dim merge, free), streamed in (2048, W) f32 blocks; grid sequential reduction.
Per element: one exp(-|x|) feeds both the sigmoid (select on sign) and log1p, then p_t, (1-p_t)^2, alpha factor, all in f32 on the VPU/EUP.
Per step the block is folded into an (8, W) f32 accumulator with VPU adds; the last step reduces it and multiplies by 1/numel.
Outside: reshape to () and astype only. Speed: one HBM pass, 2 MiB DMAs per input per step.

Grid (N, HW/4096), both arbitrary (one global accumulator); x/target viewed as (N, C, H*W), blocks (1, C, 4096) f32.
Classes sit on sublanes so the log-softmax max/sum reductions are cheap sublane reductions; CE = lse*sum(t) - sum(t*x).
f32 (1, 4096) scratch accumulates per-position CE; the last step sums it, divides by N*H*W and applies exp/(1-p)^2*logp in-kernel.
Outside: reshapes only. Speed: one streaming pass over both inputs, one exp + one log per element/position.

Grid (N, HW//th) with th up to 8192; blocks (1, C, th) for x and target (classes on sublanes, positions on lanes), about 16 MiB double-buffered under a 48 MiB VMEM limit.
Inside each step a fori_loop walks 128-lane chunks so max, exp-sum, sum(t) and sum(t*x) stay in vregs with no (C, th) VMEM temporaries; per-chunk CE goes into a loop carry.
f32 accumulator (1, 128) in VMEM scratch, resident across the whole sequential grid; the last step computes the mean CE, p=exp(-ce) and (1-p)^2*ce in-kernel.
Outside the kernel: only reshape (N,C,H,W)->(N,C,H*W) and a final reshape/astype of the (1,1) result.

Flatten x/target to (rows, 1024) f32; 1-D grid of 512-row blocks, reduction axis "arbitrary".
Two f32 (8, 1024) VMEM accumulators: weighted loss and weight; mean(loss/mean(w)) = sum(loss)/sum(w).
One exp(-|x|) feeds both the log term and the sigmoid; gamma=2 is a square.
Last step writes the scalar into a (1,128) block; outside only reshape and a [0,0] slice. Single pass, memory bound.

Grid (N, HW/4096) sequential; logits/target viewed as (N, C, H*W) with (1, 128, 4096) f32 blocks (2 MiB each).
Per block: column-wise log-sum-exp over C (sublane axis), sum_c t*l - lse*sum_c t, added to a (1, 4096) f32 VMEM accumulator.
Last step: ce = -sum/count, p = exp(-ce), loss = (1-p)^2 * ce written to a (1, 1) block; outside only reshape and astype.
Speed: one pass over both 128 MiB inputs, log_softmax never materialized.

Flatten both bf16 inputs to (rows, 512). Pad with zeros only if the size doesn't divide evenly; zeros add nothing to any of the sums. The grid has one 'arbitrary' axis over (2048, 512) bf16 row blocks: 2 inputs x 2 buffers x 2 MiB = 8 MiB of VMEM.
Inside each block, a fori_loop over 32-row chunks casts to f32 and accumulates sum(p*g), sum(g) and sum(p) into three (8,512) f32 accumulators. These carry across grid steps in a (3,8,512) f32 VMEM scratch.
The two cross terms are rewritten as sum(g)-sum(p*g) and sum(p)-sum(p*g). This cuts the per-element work to one multiply and three adds, so the kernel stays limited by memory bandwidth.
The last grid step reduces the accumulators to (1,1), then computes ti and (1-ti)^gamma as exp(gamma*log(1-ti)) inside the kernel.
Outside the kernel there are only reshape and pad, plus a final reshape of the (1,1) output to a scalar.

Grid (n,), marked parallel. Each step handles one whole sample: block (1, c, h*w), 8 MiB of f32, with x reshaped to (n, c, h*w) outside the kernel (a layout op only).
Inside the kernel, for each group: an f32 two-pass mean and variance over the resident (c/g, hw) slice. Each sum reduces along sublanes first, then along lanes. Then y = x*scale_c + shift_c, with per-channel scale and shift built from (c,1) weight and bias blocks.
Only the reshape and astype of x, weight and bias happen outside the kernel. num_groups and eps are module constants, because neither can be read from the input shapes.
Speed idea: x is read from HBM once and written once (about 256 MiB of traffic in total). The pipeline overlaps the next sample's DMA with the current step's work. vmem_limit is raised to 100 MiB so the double-buffered 8 MiB blocks plus temporaries fit.

Prep pallas_call: padded weight laid out (6,6,O,I) -> applies the scale and the 2x2 blur in-kernel, writes bf16 per-row-parity weight matrices W0 (5O, 3I) and W1 (5O, 2I). Rows are (b,o); columns are (row tap j, i).
Main pallas_call: grid (N, ceil(Y/8)), both axes "arbitrary". Input x is laid out (N, Hp, C, W) in bf16 (transpose, pad and astype outside). The whole padded image stays resident per n; each step makes 8 output rows.
Step: Z_py = W_py @ [stacked shifted input rows] (lane width 4*W, f32 accumulate, cast to bf16). Rows are regrouped to L (8*O, 5*W). A 0/1 matrix P (5W, 2W+3 rounded up to 128), built once with iota, then does the stride-2 column spread and shift in one matmul, R = L @ P with f32 accumulation.
R rows are (r,o). They are put into the NCHW output block (1,O,8,259) with sublane-strided ref reads of 8 rows per o; the bias is read from SMEM and added there. Last partial row block is clipped by Pallas.
Outside the kernels: only transpose, pad, astype and reshape. Speed: bf16 MXU work of about 0.9 GFLOP per step, output written once in its final layout, no transpose afterwards.

Reshape inputs to (B, C, S=H*W) (pad S with zeros to a multiple of 128 if needed). Grid (B, S/ts), both axes sequential. Blocks are (1, C, ts) bf16, with ts chosen so each block is about 2 MiB or less (8 MiB total with double buffering).
Inside the kernel, a static loop over 32-row channel chunks sits around a fori_loop over 128-lane column chunks. It upcasts to f32 and keeps three (rc,128) f32 running sums of t, x*t and x+t, then adds them into three (C,128) f32 VMEM scratch accumulators.
On the last grid step it reduces across lanes to per-channel sums, then computes the weights 1/max(ts^2, smooth), the intersect, the denominator and the final scalar, all in f32. The result is written to a (1,1) f32 output.
Outside the kernel there is only reshape/pad, plus reshaping the output to a scalar. The kernel is memory bound: a single pass over the 128 MB of bf16 input.

Flatten x to (N/1024, 1024) lane-dense rows; grid over 512-row blocks (1 MiB bf16 per block), 1-D parallel grid.
Elementwise math in float32 inside the kernel, cast to bf16 on store.
Outside the kernel only reshape (flatten and restore shape).
Memory bound: one read and one write of x, big lane-dense blocks to keep DMA efficient.

Flatten x to (rows, 1024) lane-dense slabs; 1D grid over rows with (1024, 1024) blocks (2 MiB bf16, about 8 MiB double-buffered in+out).
The math runs in the input dtype (bf16), so the v6e VPU/EUP process packed 16x128 vregs. The previous f32 upcast halved throughput and made the kernel compute-bound.
The formula is rewritten as h = 0.5x, out = h + h*tanh(x*(c + c*a*x^2)): one tanh and about 6 VALU ops per element, no accumulator needed.
Only the reshape stays outside the kernel. vmem_limit is raised to 48 MiB to leave headroom for intermediates.

Flatten x to (N/1024, 1024) lane-dense rows; grid over 512-row blocks (2 MiB f32 per block), 1-D parallel grid.
Elementwise math in float32 inside the kernel, cast to the input dtype on store.
Outside the kernel only reshape (flatten and restore shape).
Memory bound: one read and one write of x, big lane-dense blocks to keep DMA efficient.

Flatten x to (rows, 1024) lane-dense; grid over 512-row blocks (2 MiB f32 per block, ~8 MiB double-buffered in+out), parallel axis.
Inside each block a fori_loop walks 16-row chunks so temporaries stay in vregs instead of spilling to VMEM.
Math in f32: 0.5*x*(1+tanh(u)) rewritten as x*sigmoid(2u) = x * approx_reciprocal(1+exp(-2u)), using the EUP rather than a VPU tanh expansion.
Outside the kernel only reshape. The op is memory bound, so the goal is enough compute headroom to stream at HBM bandwidth.

Flatten x to (rows, 1024) bf16; grid over row blocks of 1024 rows (2 MiB per block).
Pure elementwise relu (leak=0, sub=0, max=inf make the other branches no-ops); no accumulator.
Only reshapes outside the kernel.
Speed: one HBM read and one write, lane-dense 1024-wide blocks, parallel grid.

View x as (N, C, HW) = (16, 128, 16384); grid (N, HW/2048), both parallel, (128, 2048) f32 blocks (1 MiB) holding all channels of a pixel strip.
In f32: channel means of x+eps and log(x+eps) via sublane reductions, closed-form k, then 10 unrolled Newton steps on the (1, 2048) strip.
lax.digamma has no Mosaic lowering, so digamma is the 6-step recurrence plus asymptotic series; trigamma as in the reference.
Outside only reshapes. Cost is one log per input element plus a small per-pixel Newton tail; memory bound on the single read.

Reshape x to (B, 2, half*H*W/1024, 1024); the same array is passed twice with index maps picking the tanh half and the gate half.
Grid (B, row blocks of 512), blocks (512, 1024) f32 = 2 MiB each; f32 math, no accumulator needed.
Outside only reshapes.
Memory bound: reads x once and writes half of it, lane-dense blocks.

Grid (B, rows/512); x is reshaped (free, layout only) to (B, 2, rows, 1024) and passed twice. One BlockSpec picks the tanh half (index 0), the other picks the gate half (index 1). The output block is (512, 1024).
Math is done in f32 inside the kernel. sigmoid(g) is computed as 0.5*tanh(0.5*g)+0.5, so each element costs two EUP tanh ops and no f32 divide. I think the divide in jax.nn.sigmoid was what made the previous kernel compute-bound instead of memory-bound.
Each 2 MiB block is double-buffered for 2 inputs and 1 output, about 12 MiB, plus temporaries, so vmem_limit is raised to 64 MiB.
Only reshapes happen outside the kernel. Both grid axes are parallel.

reshape x (B, C, H, W) -> (B, 2, R, L) with L=1024 lanes (layout only); the two channel halves are the same array passed twice.
grid=(B, R // tr), blocks (1, 1, tr, L) for the tanh half (index 0) and the sigmoid half (index 1), ~2 MiB f32 each; output (1, tr, L).
elementwise in f32 inside the kernel: tanh(a) * (0.5 * tanh(0.5 * b) + 0.5) (sigmoid via one tanh -> 2 EUP ops per output).
nothing but reshapes outside the kernel; purely HBM-bound, so large lane-dense blocks and one read of x / one write of out.

Flatten x to (N/1024, 1024); grid over 512-row blocks (1 MiB bf16), parallel.
The four scalar parameters are cast to f32 and concatenated into a (4,) SMEM operand; clamping happens on the scalar core in the kernel.
Element math in f32 (two exps, select), cast to bf16 on store. The two wheres of the reference are complementary, so one select.
Outside only reshape/astype/concatenate. Memory bound: one read, one write.

Flatten x to (rows/16, 16, 1024) bf16; grid over leading dim with (64, 16, 1024) blocks (2 MiB), parallel semantics.
Params go to SMEM as 4 f32 scalars and are clipped inside the kernel, then turned into bf16 (16, 1024) tiles so broadcasting along the leading dim costs nothing.
Elementwise math in bf16 (twice the elements per vreg on v6e). Choosing sigma before the exp means one exp per element instead of two.
Outside the kernel: only reshape, astype and concatenate of the scalar params.

Elementwise, memory-bound. Flatten x to a lane-dense 2D (rows, W) with W in {2048,1024,512,256,128} dividing the total (pad fallback otherwise); 1-D parallel grid over rows with ~2 MiB f32 blocks (in+out double-buffered ~8 MiB VMEM).
The 4 scalar params are packed into a (4,) f32 array (reshape/concatenate/astype only) and passed in SMEM; clipping happens inside the kernel.
Kernel: f32 math, one exp per element: sigma=where(x<mu,s1,s2), e=exp(-sigma*d2), out=where(x<mu, a*e, 1+(a-1)*e), cast on store.
Outside the kernel: only reshape/pad/slice/concatenate/astype.

flatten x to a lane-dense 2D slab (N/1024, 1024); grid over row blocks of 1024 rows (2 MiB bf16 per block).
compute in f32 inside the kernel: y = exp((x - mu)^2 * (-1 / (2 sigma^2))), cast to bf16 on store.
outside only reshape and astype of the scalars mu/sigma to (1,1) f32 and reshape of x / output.
speed: single fused pass, memory bound (one read + one write of x), big lane-dense blocks.

Flatten x to (N/1024, 1024); grid over 512-row blocks (1 MiB bf16), parallel.
The four scalar parameters are cast to f32 and concatenated into a (4,) SMEM operand; clamping happens on the scalar core in the kernel.
Element math in f32 (two exps, select), cast to bf16 on store.
Outside only reshape/astype/concatenate. Memory bound: one read, one write.

Flatten x to (rows, 1024) bf16; grid over 1024-row blocks (2 MiB each), parallel; params as 4 f32 scalars in SMEM, clipped in-kernel.
Inside each block a fori_loop over 16-row chunks keeps f32 temporaries in vregs (avoids VMEM spill of whole-block intermediates).
Single exp per element: select -gamma_l/-gamma_r by (x<mu), then out = where(m, a*e, 1+(a-1)*e); f32 math, cast to bf16 on store.
Outside the kernel only reshape/concatenate/astype of the scalar params and reshape of x.

Pass 1: one elementwise pallas_call computes var = exp(logvar) for both inputs on (N*D/128, 128) rows (avgpool with kern=1 is the identity).
Pass 2: grid (N, D/(512*128) j-blocks, D/2048 i-blocks), all sequential. i-side mu/var come in as 2048-scalar SMEM blocks, j-side as (512, 128) f32 VMEM blocks.
For each (8, 128) j vreg, a fori_loop over the 2048 i scalars accumulates overlap(aa) + overlap(bb) - 2*overlap(ab) for the same (i, j) pair into a vreg carry, then into an (8, 128) f32 VMEM accumulator; the last step reduces it to the scalar.
overlap = exp(-0.5*d^2/s)*rsqrt(s): 2 EUP ops per term instead of div+log+exp; combining the three sums per pair avoids cancelling 5e11-sized totals.
Outside only reshape/astype and the final [0, 0] slice. Compute bound: 16*D^2 pair evaluations (about 1e9 vreg iterations).

View x as (B*C, H*W); grid (rows/32, cols/16384), blocks (32, 16384) bf16 (1 MiB).
In-kernel: clamp in bf16 (as the reference), upcast, cube, lane-reduce into a (32,1) f32 scratch resident across the column axis.
Last column step: mean, cube root via exp(log(m)/3), cast to bf16; output (B*C,1) reshaped to (B,C,1,1) outside.
Speed: one streaming pass over 128 MiB, reduction axis innermost so the accumulator never leaves VMEM.

View prediction/target as (B*C, H*W) = (2048, 16384) so each row has one class weight; grid over 16-row blocks (1 MiB f32 each), sequential.
Class weights enter as a (16, 1) block broadcast along lanes. Loss and positive count accumulate in two (8, 16384) f32 VMEM scratches via sublane-group adds.
Last step reduces both and writes sum / max(1, count) as a (1, 1) block; outside only reshapes.
Memory bound: one pass over both inputs.

Grid (rows//br,) over (batch*channels, h*w) rows, with each block (br, h*w) about 2 MiB per input. The w block is (br, 1).
Inside the kernel, nested fori_loops walk (8, 512) chunks that stay in registers. The old version built full-block temporaries that spilled to VMEM; this avoids that.
The unweighted per-row loss is accumulated first and multiplied by w once per 8-row group, which removes the per-element lane broadcast.
Accumulators are f32 (8, cw) VMEM scratch, carried across grid steps and reduced once at the last step. The minus sign and the division by max(1, npos) are done in-kernel.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes.

Grid (R/bm,) over the flattened rows (R = 524288, n = 128). The input block is (bm=8192, 128) bf16, about 2 MiB per step and about 4 MiB double-buffered.
The kernel upcasts to f32 and computes log(max(x, 0)). It sums each row of the f32 log values with ones(8,n) . L^T on the MXU, contracting the last dims, which gives a lane-dense (8, bm) result. The log values are split into bf16 hi and lo parts so the sum stays close to f32 precision, and the matmul accumulates in f32.
The kernel then applies exp(sum/n) and stores a lane-dense (1, bm) bf16 row into an output of shape (G, 1, bm).
Outside the kernel there are only two reshapes: input to (R, n) and output back to x.shape[:-1].
Speed: one read of the input and lane-dense stores, with the reduction moved off the XLU onto the MXU.

Reshape x,y to (B,C,HW); lane tile tk (largest of 4096..128 dividing HW, capped so blocks stay ~2 MiB). Kernel 1: grid (B, HW/tk), "parallel","arbitrary"; f32 (C,128) VMEM accumulator of x+y using static 128-lane slices; on the last step it reduces over lanes, divides by HW, and computes att = sigmoid(W^T @ pooled + bias) on the MXU with f32 accumulation, giving an att output of shape (B,C,1).
Kernel 2: grid (B, HW/tk), both parallel; out = y + (x-y)*att, with att broadcast along lanes.
Outside: only reshapes, a transpose of the weight and a reshape of the bias. Memory traffic is the same as XLA's fused version (read x,y twice, write once) with lane-dense blocks.

x reshaped to (B, C, H*W); grid (B, HW/tk) with (1, C, tk) bf16 blocks of ~2 MiB, tk a multiple of 128.
f32 (C, 128) VMEM scratch holds lane-group partial sums across the "arbitrary" HW axis.
Last HW step: lane-reduce to the (C, 1) mean, then mean*w summed over C plus bias gives the (1, N) row in f32, cast to bf16.
Only reshapes outside. Memory bound on the single read of x; the tiny FC is done on the VPU once per batch row.

x reshaped to (N, C, H*W); grid (N, HW/tk) with (1, C, 4096) bf16 blocks (1 MiB); w (C, 8) and b (1, 8) whole.
Spatial sum accumulated in a (C, 128) f32 VMEM scratch by adding 128-lane chunks (VPU only, no per-step XLU reduce).
Last k step: lane-reduce to pooled (C,1), pooled*w summed over C gives (1,8), + b, tanh, cast to bf16.
Outside only reshapes ((N,1,8) -> (N,4,2)). Speed idea: memory-bound single pass over x; the tiny linear rides along.

Flatten x to (rows, 1024) f32; grid over row blocks of 512 rows (2 MiB per block, 8 MiB double-buffered in+out).
Elementwise nested select in f32; no accumulator.
Only reshapes outside the kernel.
Speed: memory bound, one read and one write with lane-dense blocks and a parallel grid.

Flatten x (layout-only reshape) to (rows, L), where L is the largest of 1024/512/256/128 that divides x.size. If none divides it, L is the last dim (full-dim block).
Grid is cdiv(rows, br) with blocks of about 2 MiB, so br*L*4B ≈ 2 MiB (512x1024 for f32). br is a multiple of 8, or all the rows when there are fewer than that. In + out with double buffering is about 8 MiB of VMEM.
Kernel: clip(x + 3, 0, 6) * (1/6), computed in f32 and cast to the output dtype on store. No accumulator is needed.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes. The grid axis is marked "parallel".
The work is memory-bound, so large lane-dense tiles should keep HBM reads and writes near XLA's fused-elementwise speed.

Flatten x to a lane-dense 2D view (rows, 1024) when the total size divides by 1024; otherwise use (prod(leading dims), last dim). This is a reshape only.
Grid is 1-D over row blocks: 512 rows x 1024 lanes of f32 is 2 MiB per block. With input and output double-buffered that is about 8 MiB, under the 16 MiB scoped VMEM. The grid uses pl.cdiv, so a partial last block is masked by Pallas.
The kernel computes x * clip(x+3, 0, 6) * (1/6) in f32 and casts back to the input dtype on store. There is no reduction and no accumulator.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes. The work is limited by HBM bandwidth; large lane-dense blocks and a "parallel" grid axis keep the copy-in/copy-out near peak speed.

Grid (B, cdiv(Ho, 32)); x main block (1, Cin, 32, W) bf16 plus a 16-row halo block below, native NCHW; output block
(1, Cout, 32, Wo) bf16 (last block partial). Hyper params t*hyper_w + hyper_b are computed in-kernel once (float32,
then bf16) into a (3*Cout, 3*Cin) weight scratch; outside only slice/reshape/transpose of hyper_w/hyper_b.
Rows are upcast into an f32 scratch, gathered as (Cin, W) via sublane-strided loads, and two output rows per matmul:
weights (dx,co | dy,ci) @ 3 stacked rows for each of the pair (384 x 256), float32 accumulation; the 3 dx partials
are lane-rolled and summed with the bias, written by strided stores to an f32 (Cout, 32, W) scratch, then cast.
Speed: K=384, M=384, N=256 matmuls (~77 GFLOP); one pass over x (+50% halo) and the output.

Three chained pallas_calls, one per ConvTranspose, in NHWC (leading H, sublane W, lane C). Grid (B, H/qh) with qh=8 input rows for the stride-2 layers and 16 for the final layer; 1-row prev/next margin blocks are masked at the edges.
Each of the k*k taps is a bf16 (rows*W, Cin) @ (Cin, Cout) matmul accumulated in f32, grouped by output parity. Stride-2 layers interleave parity subgrids through an f32 VMEM scratch using leading-index and sublane-strided stores, then add bias, apply ReLU and cast to bf16.
Outside the kernels: only transposes and a bias reshape. Stride is a module-level constant passed per layer because shapes cannot give it; padding is derived as (k-1)//2. vmem_limit_bytes is raised to 64 MiB (spills and weights can exceed 16 MiB).
Speed idea: margin blocks avoid re-reading whole neighbour tiles, weights stay resident, and bf16 keeps HBM traffic low. Not compiled or run here; the sublane-strided store is the main compile risk.

The stride is a plain strided slice outside the kernel (an allowed layout op, and a no-op when stride is 1), then a reshape to (B, C, H*W) so blocks are lane-dense.
Grid (B, HW/t), both axes parallel. Input block is (1, Cin, t), output block is (1, Cout, t). t is the largest multiple of 128 that divides H*W with a block of at most about 2 MiB; if H*W is not a multiple of 128, t is the full H*W.
The kernel copies x into output channels [:Cin] and writes zeros to [Cin:]; the zero-fill is skipped when add is 0. No accumulator is needed because this is pure data movement in bf16.
Double-buffered VMEM use is about 8 MiB. The speed idea is large lane-dense blocks so the copy runs at HBM bandwidth.
ADD_CHANNELS and STRIDE are module constants that mirror the reference, because neither can be taken from the input shape.

Grid (B*C/8,), block (8, H*W) f32 = 2 MiB on the (B*C, H*W) view; in+out double-buffered 8 MiB.
No accumulator; the channel pad has zero width at these sizes, so the kernel is a straight copy.
Outside: only reshape to/from the 2D view.
Speed: one HBM read and one write with wide lane-dense blocks, same as XLA's copy.

No grid: x and the output stay in HBM (pl.ANY); the kernel starts up to 8 async DMAs (contiguous leading-dim slices) and waits on them.
No accumulator, no VMEM tiles; the channel pad has zero width at these shapes (out_channels is not recoverable from the inputs).
Outside the kernel: nothing; native NCHW layout in and out, so no relayout copies.
Speed idea: one HBM read + one write through the DMA engines, matching XLA's copy.

Input viewed as (2B*C, HW/2) (the torch view), output as (2B*C, H*W): row r of the output is the mean of input row r broadcast.
Grid (R/64,), input block (64, HW/2) bf16, output block (64, H*W) bf16; mean in f32 via lane reduction, broadcast across lanes, cast on store.
No accumulator beyond the per-row sum; outside only reshapes (final reshape to (-1, oc, H, W)).
Speed: memory bound, input read once and the 2x larger output written once, lane-dense stores.

sequential grid (E/TE + 1,), TE = 2048 edges per block; edge ids arrive as a (2, TE) int32 SMEM block per step; output (1, E) bf16 in (1, TE) blocks.
z is cast to f32 outside (astype only) and stays in HBM (pl.ANY); step i issues 2*TE single-row DMAs gathering z[src], z[dst] for block i into a double-buffered (2, TE, D) f32 VMEM slot.
step i then waits on block i-1 (one bulk wait per buffer) and reduces it: P = A*B in f32, transpose to (D, TE), sublane sum -> lane-dense (1, TE), sigmoid, cast to bf16.
speed: the DMA gather of block i overlaps the reduction of block i-1, and no (E, D) gathered intermediates go through HBM (XLA materializes two).

Grid (B*C/8,), block (8, H*W) over x reshaped to (B*C, H*W): each row is one (b, c) instance, fully resident.
f32 math: row mean, centered mean square, multiply by rsqrt(var + eps); two passes over the tile in VMEM.
Outside the kernel only reshapes.
Speed idea: one HBM read and one write of x (memory bound), lane-dense 65536-wide rows.

View x as (B, C, HW) (layout only); grid (B, C // CB) with CB channels per step so a (CB, HW) block is ~2 MiB; scale/shift as (C, 1).
Whole spatial row lives in VMEM, so one HBM read + one write: per 8-row group compute sum(x), sum(x*x) in f32 lane reductions.
var = E[x^2] - E[x]^2 (as the reference), a = scale * rsqrt(var + eps), c = shift - mean * a, out = x * a + c, cast on store.
Only reshapes stay outside the kernel; both grid axes are parallel; speed comes from fusing stats + normalize into a single pass.

Grid (batch, channels // cb) with cb the largest divisor of channels keeping double-buffered input <= 8 MiB (cb=4 at 512x512); parallel on both axes.
Input block (1, cb, H, W); four output blocks (1, cb, 65, 65), (1, cb, 32, 32), (1, cb, 17, 17), (1, cb, 8, 8), each full in the last two dims.
Both init pools are fused into one 4x4 stride-4 max of 16 strided loads; each later stage is a max of 4 stride-2 loads.
Padded stages use small f32 VMEM scratches of (h+2, w+2) with a -inf border, so edge windows need no special case. Unpadded stages read the previous output ref.
All values stay in x.dtype (f32) with no matmuls; nothing runs outside the kernel except the pallas_call itself. Not run on TPU here.

grid over output rows in tb=2048-row blocks (parallel); out block (tb, 2*Du+Db) bf16, binary block (tb, Db) via BlockSpec.
index1/index2 come in per-block (tb,) int32 SMEM blocks; unary stays in HBM (pl.ANY) and every gathered row is one
row DMA HBM -> VMEM scratch (tb, Du); all 2*tb row copies are issued first, then one aggregate wait per buffer.
outside: only unary.astype(f32) (dtype op) so single-row DMAs are 32-bit (no packed bf16 sublane halves); the cast
back to bf16 is exact. In-kernel: the three lane-aligned stores build the concat [u1 | u2 | binary] in one pass.

Grid (B, HW/tn) arbitrary; both embeddings viewed as (B, C, H*W), blocks (1, C, 2048) f32 = 1 MiB each.
Per column: L2 norms over C (sublane reduction), normalize, squared difference summed over C into a (1, tn) f32 scratch.
Last step reduces the scratch into a (1, 128) output; the scalar slice is outside.
Speed: one memory-bound pass over 268 MB, norms computed once per column.

Keep k, v in their (T, B, D) layout; grid over T chunks of 32, blocks (32, B, D) bf16, everything else resident full blocks.
Per time step t: k[t] (B,K) x key_w on the MXU (f32 accumulate) + precomputed q projection, tanh, then the logit both as a (B,1) column (lane reduce) and a (1,B) row (NT matmul).
Column logits drive an online softmax (running max/sum, f32 (B,V) accumulator) for the value sum; row logits fill a (T,1,B) f32 scratch, softmaxed over T at the last step.
Outside: astype/reshape of the small biases and a reshape + transpose of the (T,B) probabilities into (B,T).
Speed: one pass over k and v (64 MiB) with no swapaxes copies and no (B,T,H) intermediate in HBM.

Reshape output/target (layout only) to (N=b*j, D=h*w); grid (N//R, D//C) with R=256, C=2048 bf16 blocks (1 MiB each, about 4 MiB when double-buffered). Both grid axes are "arbitrary" because one accumulator is resident across the whole grid.
Weight is passed twice after an astype to f32: as an (N,1) column blocked by rows for the per-row broadcast, and as a full (b,j) block for the normalizer.
Inside each block a fori_loop walks 16-row chunks. Each chunk computes w*(g-p)^2 in f32, then exp(0.1*log(d))*thr^0.9 where d > thr, and folds into an (8,C) f32 carry. The carry is added to a VMEM (8,C) f32 scratch.
On the last grid step the kernel reduces the scratch and divides by D*max(1, sum(w)), writing a (1,1) f32 output. Outside the kernel there is only reshape/astype; the op is memory-bound, so the input HBM reads are the single pass.

Flatten fake/real to (rows, 1024) f32; 1-D grid over 512-row blocks (2 MiB each), reduction axis "arbitrary".
f32 (8, 1024) VMEM accumulator: each block is summed over its leading row groups with plain vreg adds.
Last step does the cross-lane sum and the divide by the element count; outside only reshape and a [0, 0] slice.
Speed: single pass over both inputs, memory bound.

Flatten the inputs to a lane-dense (rows, 1024) layout outside the kernel (reshape only; falls back to (rows, W) if the size isn't divisible by 1024).
1D 'arbitrary' grid over row blocks of up to 512 rows (2 MiB per input block; 2 inputs x 2 buffers = 8 MiB VMEM).
Each step folds sqrt(d*d+eps^2) into an (8, L) f32 VMEM scratch with plain vector adds (reshape(bm//8,8,L).sum(0)); a ragged tail is masked in-kernel with iota.
On the last step, reduce the scratch to a scalar, multiply by 1/N, and write a (1,1) output; outside the kernel only reshape to a scalar.
Speed: memory-bound job done as one fused pass that reads each input from HBM once with large blocks.

Grid (rows/4096,) sequential; fake and real viewed as (size/128, 128) with (4096, 128) f32 blocks (2 MiB).
f32 |log r - log f| folded into an (8, 128) f32 VMEM accumulator; last step sums to (1, 1) and scales by 1/size.
Shapes are equal for this task, so no resize; outside only reshape to () and astype.
Speed: one streaming pass over both inputs, single final cross-lane reduce.

Grid (N, H*W/ts) over x reshaped to (N, C, H*W); block (1, C, ts) with ts ~ 2048 lanes (1 MiB f32); weight as (C, 1) resident block.
Sum of squares over the channel (sublane) axis in float32, sqrt + eps, one reciprocal per pixel, multiply by x and per-channel weight.
Outside the kernel: reshapes only.
Speed: HBM-bound single pass, lane-dense tiles, both grid axes parallel.

Grid (N0,) over the first axis, one step per output slice x[g,:,:,:]; all blocks are 0.5 MiB bf16, about 3 MiB VMEM double-buffered.
The reference's divisor is d[h,c,g] = sqrt(sum_c' x[h,c',c,g]^2), since .T makes div align as (h,c,b), so it needs a slice along the last axis of x.
Outside the kernel there is only a layout op: x2 = x.transpose(3,2,0,1), so x2[g,c,h,c'] = x[h,c',c,g] and block (1,N2,N0,N1) holds the reduction axis in lanes.
Inside, the sum over axis -1 with keepdims gives (c,h,1), which broadcasts directly over the output (c,h,w) with no in-kernel relayout. All arithmetic is f32, cast to bf16 on store.
Speed idea: one fused pass, at the cost of one 33 MB transpose. Not compiled or run here, so the speed ratio and Mosaic acceptance are untested.

flatten x to a lane-dense 2D view (rows, L) with L in {1024,512,256,128}; grid over row blocks (bm ~ 2048 rows, 4 MiB bf16).
inside each step a fori_loop over 32-row chunks: relu, upcast to f32, square, fold into an (8,L) f32 carry (pure VPU adds).
(8,L) f32 VMEM scratch accumulator resident across the "arbitrary" grid axis; last step does full sum + sqrt in-kernel.
outside only reshape + astype of the (1,1) result to x.dtype; single HBM pass, memory-bound.

Grid (N*C/8,), input block (8*H, W) = 8 whole images as rows of a 2D view; output block (1, W/8, 8*H/8).
Three 2x2/2 pools collapse to one 8x8/8 pool: 8 sublane-strided loads (stride 8) give the row max,
then one in-VMEM transpose and 8 more strided loads give the column max. f32 compare, no accumulator.
Outside: free reshape of the input, and a transpose of the tiny pooled output (1/64 of input) back to NCHW.
Speed: one HBM pass over the 256 MB input, all pooling in VMEM.

Grid (B,) 'parallel'; one block (1, C, H, W) bf16 per sample in native layout (4 MiB), vmem limit raised for double buffering.
Pass 1 (fori over channels): per-channel mean and centred sum of squares in f32 into (C, 128) VMEM scratch.
Layer mean/var come from the channel stats exactly (sum ss_c + n*sum (m_c - M)^2), unbiased (ddof=1); rho, gamma, beta fold into per-channel scale a_c and shift b_c.
Pass 2 (fori over channels): out = x*a_c + b_c in f32, rounded once to bf16. Outside: only reshapes/astype of the (1, C, 1, 1) parameters.
Speed: x read from HBM once, written once (2 passes over VMEM), instead of XLA's separate mean/var/normalise passes.

Two pallas_calls on the (N, C, H*W) view, grid (N, HW/4096), blocks (1, C, 4096) bf16.
Pass 1 accumulates per-sample sum and sum of squares in f32 into resident (1, 1, 128) output blocks.
Pass 2 turns the raw sums into mean / rsqrt(var + eps) in-kernel and applies (x - mean) * rstd * gamma + beta, gamma/beta as (C, 1) f32.
Outside: only reshapes and the f32 cast of gamma/beta. Speed: 2 reads + 1 write of x, memory bound like XLA.

Grid (n,), with one whole sample per step: x is viewed as (n, C, HW/128, 128) and the block is (1, C, HW/128, 128). In bf16 that is 16 MiB, so 64 MiB with double-buffered input and output, and vmem_limit is set to 100 MiB.
Inside the kernel, pass 1 runs a fori_loop over (channel, row-chunk) slices of up to 512x128 and accumulates sum and sum-of-squares into f32 (8,128) partials using only VPU adds.
The two partials are then reduced to mean and rstd. Pass 2 re-reads the sample from VMEM and writes x*a_c + b_c, where a_c = gamma_c*rstd and b_c = beta_c - mean*a_c are per-channel scalars, with gamma and beta in SMEM.
This reads HBM once and writes it once (256 MB of traffic), compared with 384 MB for the old two-call version and for XLA's fused path.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes and the f32 astype of gamma and beta.

Two pallas_calls over the native layout with blocks (1, 2, 256, F) float32 (2 MiB), grid (D0, D1/2).
Call 1 (sequential): fori_loop over 8-row chunks accumulates x^2 into an (8, F) float32 scratch, writes sum(x^2) as (1,1).
Call 2: takes that (1,1) sum, computes sqrt(4*F/sum) in-kernel, then per 8-row chunk the row mean, unbiased std
(lane reductions, float32) and writes to_norm * (x - mean) / (std + eps). Nothing but astype outside.
Speed: the global norm forces two passes; 3x the tensor in HBM traffic, same as the fused XLA plan.

Grid (N, HW/T) over the (N, C, H*W) view, block (1, C, T) with T*C*4 = 1 MB, all f32.
Channel reduction is over sublanes (axis 0 of the block): two-pass mean/var in registers, rsqrt, affine with (C, 1) weight/bias.
Outside: free reshapes and the f32 cast of weight/bias only.
Speed: one read and one write of x, lane-dense blocks, both grid axes parallel.

Grid (N, HWp/T) with blocks (1, C, T) and T about 2^19/C lanes (2 MiB f32 tiles, 32 steps at the given sizes), both axes parallel, vmem_limit set to 48 MiB.
Inside the kernel a fori_loop walks 128-lane strips (C x 128 values in vregs). Per strip it computes mean, variance and rsqrt over the channel (sublane) axis in f32, then the affine. No full-tile temporaries are written back to VMEM.
Weight and bias are cast to f32 and broadcast to (C, 128) outside the kernel (layout only), so each strip does a plain vector load instead of a lane broadcast.
Outside the kernel: reshape NCHW to (N, C, HW), pad to a multiple of 128 lanes only if needed, then slice and reshape back. No float arithmetic happens outside.

Grid (N, HW/T) over the (N, C, H*W) view, block (1, C, T) with T*C*4 = 1 MB, all f32.
Channel reduction is over sublanes (axis 0 of the block): two-pass mean/var in registers, rsqrt, affine with (C, 1) weight/bias.
Outside: free reshapes and the f32 cast of weight/bias only.
Speed: one read and one write of x, lane-dense blocks, both grid axes parallel.

Reshape NCHW to (N, C, HW). Grid (N, HW/T) with block (1, C, T), T chosen so a block is about 4 MiB (T=4096 for C=256), giving 64 grid steps instead of 256.
Inside the kernel a fori_loop walks 256-lane chunks so intermediates stay at about 64 vregs. It does a two-pass mean/var in f32 over the sublane (channel) axis, applies rsqrt, then the affine.
gamma and beta are broadcast outside to (C, chunk) f32, which is a layout op only, so the kernel needs no lane broadcast.
vmem_limit is raised to 64 MiB: 2x in + 2x out = 16 MiB of buffers plus small params. Only reshape, broadcast and astype run outside the kernel.

Two pallas_calls over x reshaped (N, rows, 1024) f32 with (1, 512, 1024) blocks, grid (N, rows/512).
Pass 1: per-sample sum of x^2 in an f32 (8, 1024) VMEM accumulator, last step writes 1/sqrt(mean+eps) as a (1,1,128) block.
Pass 2: elementwise x * inv with the per-sample factor broadcast from its (1,1,128) block.
Outside only reshapes. Speed: 2 reads + 1 write of x, the same traffic as XLA's reduce + elementwise fusions.

Grid (M/2048, P/256, K/512): x block (2048, 512) f32 cast to bf16 in-kernel, permuted w1 block (512, 1024) bf16, w2 block (256, 1024) bf16.
w1 columns are permuted outside (reshape/transpose, plus bf16 cast) so each pool window of 4 becomes 4 lane-aligned 256-wide slabs.
f32 (2048, 1024) accumulator; at the last K step, max over the 4 slabs gives pooled (2048, 256), then pooled @ w2_tile is added into the f32 output block, resident across j and k.
Speed idea: the max-pool and second matmul are fused into the first GEMM's epilogue; h (64 MB) never reaches HBM.

Grid (m/1024, pdim/512, K/1024): x block (1024,1024) f32 cast to bf16 in-kernel, w1p block (1024, 2048) bf16, w2 block (512, nout) bf16; (1024, 2048) f32 acc scratch, (1024, nout) f32 output block resident across j and k.
At the last k: max over the 4 lane-aligned 512-column slabs (maxpool), bf16 dot with the w2 rows of this j, accumulated into the output.
Outside: w1 column permutation + bf16 cast, w2 bf16 cast (layout/dtype ops).
Speed idea vs attempt 1: bigger N and K tiles cut x re-reads 4x->2x, halve the grid steps and acc read-modify-writes per MXU FLOP.

Grid is 1-D over chunks of 8 conv rows (32 steps, sequential). Each step loads a 16-row block of x plus two 8-row neighbour blocks for the edge rows, and the matching linear_w block (64, 512, 30), which is 16 MiB once padded in VMEM.
Inside the kernel: (1) stride-2 row loads give the vertical max. (2) A 0/1 bf16 matrix built with iota does the column pairing and splits columns into even/odd streams, with the left/right shifts and zero padding built in; a max then gives four column-phase sources. (3) The 3x3 conv is one MXU matmul per batch: a banded weight (1024x256) times the sources (256x128), with rows ordered (E/O column, row parity, row, out-channel). The 2x2 pool is then a max over 4 row-slices, followed by bias and ReLU. (4) Features go into VMEM scratch. Stride-64 loads move batch onto sublanes, and the result is multiplied with the weight block (bf16 inputs, f32 result) into an (8, 30) f32 accumulator. The final bias and ReLU run on the last step.
Outside the kernel: only reshape, stack, pad, slice, transpose, broadcast and astype, used to build the banded conv weight, the per-row bias and the weight view (64, 16384, 30).
Speed idea: the linear weight is read once, in its own layout; all other compute overlaps its DMA.

Grid over row-chunks of the pooled image (Hp/8 steps, arbitrary). Each step loads B*C x 16 x W input rows plus 8-row halo blocks. It does the first maxpool on the VPU and the column pool and stride-select with a 0/1 selection matmul. The 3x3 conv plus second pool is a banded-weight matmul. Bias and relu are fused, and the linear partial sum goes into an f32 (B,OUT) scratch. All matmuls take bf16 inputs and accumulate in f32. Outside the kernel there are only layout ops (stack, pad, concatenate, reshape, transpose, broadcast) that build the banded conv weight and the broadcast bias. jnp.tile is now broadcast_to plus reshape.

Flatten both inputs into a lane-dense (rows, 1024) f32 slab. Pad with zeros only when the size isn't a multiple of the block. The 1-D grid runs over 512-row blocks (32 steps here); each block is 2 MiB per input, about 8 MiB of VMEM double-buffered.
In the kernel: d=|y-y'|+eps, then log(cosh d) = d + log(1+exp(-2d)) - log2 (one exp, one log, stable for large d).
Partial sums go into an (8,1024) f32 VMEM scratch, summed over the leading axis so it's plain vector adds. On the last step: one full reduction times 1/N (true element count) into a (1,1) output.
Outside the kernel: only reshape/pad/astype and a final reshape to a scalar. Zero padding gives d=eps, which rounds to 0 in f32, so it doesn't change the result. This is a streaming, memory-bound reduction.

Inputs viewed as (B*C, H, W) (leading-dim merge, free); grid over groups of 4 planes, blocks (4, 256, 256) f32.
Per step (atan(x) - atan(y))^2 in f32 (atan as a Cephes polynomial: Mosaic has no atan) folded into an (8, W) f32 VMEM accumulator; the last step reduces, divides by the element count and takes the sqrt.
Outside: only the leading-dim reshape and the (1,1) -> scalar reshape.
Speed: single memory-bound pass over both 134 MB inputs.

Grid (N*C/16,) over the (N*C, H*W) view, block (16, 16384) f32 = 1 MB: each row is one full spatial map.
Per row: lane-reduced max, exp(gamma*(x - m)) summed in f32, then m + log(s / HW) / gamma, all in VMEM.
Outside: free reshapes only.
Speed: single HBM read of the input; output is 1/HW the size.

Free reshape of x to (524288, 128) f32 rows; grid over blocks of (4096, 128) rows (2 MiB), output (4096, 128) lane-dense f32.
Inside, a fori_loop takes 128-row groups, transposes each (128, 128) tile on the XLU, and reduces over sublanes: two-pass
mean and unbiased variance in f32, then log(clip(var)), written as one dense 128-lane output row per group.
Outside: only the final reshape of the (4096, 128) result to (8, 32, 64, 32, 1).
Speed: one memory-bound read of x; the transpose turns lane reductions into cheap sublane adds and keeps output stores dense.

Grid (8*32,) over the (A*B, C, R, d) view (leading-dim merge, a bitcast); block (1, 64, 32, 128) f32 = 1 MB in, output block (1, 64, 32, 1) written in the final shape so no relayout runs outside.
Row sums on the MXU: x and x*x split into bf16 hi+lo, each dotted with a ones (128,128) matrix, f32 accumulation (~2^-17 relative error), 256 rows per call; no XLU transposes.
One pass: var = (sumsq - sum^2/d)/(d-1), clip, log in f32 into a (C*R, 128) VMEM scratch whose lanes all hold the row value.
A second fori_loop stores lane 0 of each 32-row slab into the (32,1) output slab.
Outside: only reshapes that merge or split leading dims.

Grid (N, HW/2048) over (N, C, H*W) views; input blocks (1, C, 2048) f32 (1 MB each), output block (1, 1, 2048).
Clamp, multiply, mean over C as a sublane reduction, -log, all in f32 in-kernel.
Outside: free reshapes only.
Speed: one read of both inputs, lane-dense output rows; memory bound like XLA.

rows packed 4-per-row (free reshape x -> (M/4, 4*D)) with block-diagonal weights (built outside by pad/concatenate only) so the MXU sees K=512, N=144.
one pallas_call, grid (M/4/tr,), x block (tr=4096, 512) bf16; inside, a fori_loop over 512-row chunks runs all three layers on-chip (bf16 MXU operands, f32 accumulate, bias/ReLU/sigmoid in f32).
last layer computed transposed (W3p^T @ h2^T, NT dot_general) so the output block (4*O, tr) is lane-dense; outside only transpose+reshape back to (..., O).
speed: x (128 MiB) is read exactly once and nothing intermediate touches HBM, so the kernel runs near HBM bandwidth.

Reshape (B,C,H,W)->(B,C,H*W) (free, layout only). Grid (B, HW//T), blocks (1,C,T) for both inputs; T = largest multiple of 128 dividing H*W with C*T*4 <= 1 MiB (T=2048 here).
Inside the kernel: f32 softmax over the channel (sublane) axis (max, exp, sum, exact reciprocal), then (p-t)^2, folded into an (8,T) f32 VMEM scratch accumulator with plain vector adds; (1,T) fallback if C%8 != 0.
On the last grid step: sum the accumulator, multiply by 1/N, write a (1,1) output. Outside the kernel only the reshape and the scalar index of that output.
Both grid axes are "arbitrary" (the accumulator carries across steps; v6e has one TensorCore). Memory-bound: each input is read once.

Reshape to (B, C, HW); grid (B, HW//T), blocks (1, C, T) with T the largest multiple of 128 dividing HW and C*T*4 <= 4 MiB (2 inputs x 2 buffers ~16 MiB, vmem limit 48 MiB).
Inside the kernel, a fori_loop over 128-lane chunks keeps the (C,128) slice in vregs: max, exp, sum, divide, subtract, square, then fold C into (8,128) f32 partials carried through the loop.
A (8,128) f32 VMEM scratch accumulates across all grid steps (arbitrary semantics); the last step reduces it and writes the mean to a (1,1) output.
Outside the kernel: only reshape, slice and astype. Speed idea: about 4x fewer grid steps, and no full-block intermediates going through VMEM, so the kernel runs at HBM bandwidth.

Flatten both inputs (a layout reshape) to a (rows, L) 2-D view, with L=1024 when it divides the element count, otherwise the last dim. Grid over row blocks of up to 512 rows, so 2 MiB f32 per input block and about 8 MiB double-buffered.
Inside the kernel: d=o-t, sq=d*d, set entries where t==4 to zero, then fold the block into an (8, L) f32 VMEM accumulator using only vreg adds.
At the last grid step, reduce the accumulator to a scalar, divide by the total element count, and write a (1,1) f32 output. Outside the kernel there is only reshape/indexing to get a scalar.
fraction=1.0, so there is no top-k. This is a single pass over HBM, bandwidth-bound like XLA's fused reduction.

Inputs are flattened to (rows, 1024) using reshape only. The 1-D grid steps over row blocks of up to 1024x1024 f32 (4 MiB per input). Two inputs, double-buffered, need 16 MiB, so vmem_limit_bytes is raised to 64 MiB.
Inside each block, a fori_loop (unroll 4) walks 32-row chunks and keeps an (8,1024) f32 accumulator in registers. This avoids writing the full squared-error block back to VMEM. Each step adds that accumulator into a VMEM scratch.
On the last step the kernel reduces the scratch and multiplies by 1/n to get the mean. Outside the kernel there are only reshape and astype.
The previous version scored 0.66x XLA. The speed changes are bigger blocks (fewer grid steps) and the register accumulator. This version has not been run on the oracle yet.

Flatten both inputs (a layout-only reshape) to (rows, C) with C=512 when numel allows it (otherwise C=W). The grid runs over row blocks of up to about 2 MiB per input (2048x512 bf16), marked "arbitrary" because it is a reduction.
Inside the kernel, a fori_loop over 64-row chunks upcasts to f32, computes d*d and folds it into an (8, C) f32 VMEM accumulator using only elementwise VPU adds.
On the last grid step the kernel reduces the accumulator to a scalar, divides by numel, and stores a (1,1) result in the input dtype. Outside the kernel there is only a reshape to a scalar.
The kernel is bound by memory bandwidth: each input is read once and VMEM use is about 8 MiB, with the scoped limit raised to 32 MiB.

Flatten both inputs to (R, 128), zero-padding the tail only if the size is not a multiple of one block; padded elements add 0 and the divisor stays the true element count.
Grid (R // 4096,), input blocks (4096, 128) = 2 MiB each, about 8 MiB VMEM with double buffering. The tall shape keeps the expensive lane reduction to one 128-wide pass per step.
The (1, 1) f32 output block stays resident across the sequential grid as the accumulator and is zeroed at step 0. Each step adds sum(d*d) * (1 / total), so the division happens inside the kernel.
Outside the kernel: only reshape, pad, astype, and the final reshape to a scalar.
Speed: the workload is memory-bound, so one fused pass reads each input exactly once.

Grid (T/256, N/256) sequential; y_pred viewed as (T, N*C) with block (256, 256*C), y_gt as (N, T*C) with block (256, 256*C) at the transposed block index.
Channels 0/1 are de-interleaved from the minor C axis by a one-hot (128*C, 256) bf16 selector matmul per 128-position chunk (exact: one nonzero per output, f32 acc), built once from iota into scratch.
The gt tiles are transposed in VMEM (256x256 f32), squared differences of both channels fold into an (8, 256) f32 accumulator; last step reduces and divides by T*N.
Outside: free reshapes and the scalar cast to bf16. Speed: one read of each input, no HBM transpose or channel slicing copies.

Grid (B/32,) sequential; v block (32, L, F) bf16 = 1 MB, labels as a (32, 1, 1) int32 block.
Squared norms via a batched ones(8, F) x (x^2)^T MXU contraction so the result (bb, 8, L) has labels on lanes; x^2 is split into bf16 hi + lo so the sum is exact up to f32 accumulation.
One-hot from iota == label, margin terms in f32, summed over the batch axis into an (8, L) f32 scratch (8 identical rows); last step reduces and scales by 1/(8*B).
Outside: reshape of labels and the scalar cast to bf16. Speed: one read of v, no lane-sparse (L, 1) intermediates.

Reference broadcasting with S=1 gives an output of shape (B,B,L): out[i,j,l] = seq[j] if mask[i,l]==1 else 0. Outside the kernel only reshapes happen: mask (B,L)->(B,R,128), seq (B,S)->(B*S,), and the output (B,B,R,128)->(B,B,L).
Grid is (B, R//tr), both axes parallel. The mask block is (1,tr,128) and the output block is (1,B,tr,128); with tr=1024 that is 512KB in and 4MB out, about 9MB double-buffered. The VMEM limit is raised to 48MB.
seq sits in SMEM as scalars. The kernel computes the compare once per tile and writes B selects, so it is pure HBM-write bound: one read of the mask and a lane-dense write of the output.
There is no matmul, so no accumulator is needed. The output dtype is the seq dtype.

Flatten all three inputs to a lane-dense 2-D view (R, 1024), falling back to (R, W) if the total isn't divisible by 1024. Grid is 1-D over row blocks of up to 1024 rows (4 MiB per input block), with dimension semantics "arbitrary".
Each step computes the SmoothL1 loss on the VPU in f32 and folds it into an (8, C) f32 VMEM accumulator using adds across vregs only.
The last step reduces the accumulator to a scalar, multiplies by 1/N and writes a (1,1) output block. Outside the kernel there is only reshape and the final reshape to ().
Speed: one HBM pass over the 400 MB of input, with large blocks to amortize per-step overhead. vmem_limit is raised to 48 MiB to fit 3 inputs x 2 buffers x 4 MiB.

view x as (B*C, H, W); grid (B*C/cb,), x block (cb, H, W) f32 (~8 MiB, cb=32 here), out block (cb, 2H) f32.
per channel: fold W's 128-lane slabs elementwise (max, and count of x>0 in f32) into two (H, 128) tiles,
transpose each (XLU) and reduce over sublanes so H lands on lanes: max -> out[:, :H], count/W -> out[:, H:2H].
outside the kernel only reshapes ((B*C,2H) -> (B,C,1,2H)); all compares/max/sum/divide happen in-kernel.
speed: single streaming pass over x with big blocks, nearly pure VPU work hidden under the HBM DMA.

Grid (B*C/8,), input block (8, H, W) f32, output block (8, H/2, W/2); a (W, W/2) bf16 one-hot selector built in-kernel from iota.
Rows: stride-2 sublane loads give rows 2i and 2i+1; a sublane roll gives 2i-1 (masked at i=0: -inf for max, 0 for sum).
Columns: lane rolls give c-1/c+1 at full width, masked at c=0; fused max + sum/9 in f32.
Even-column pick on the MXU as hi+lo bf16 matmuls with f32 accumulate (near-exact). Outside only reshapes.
Speed: one read of x, quarter-size write, no padded copy; both pools fused.

grid (HW/128,), input block (N, C, 128) f32 = 2 MiB (whole batch and all channels of a pixel strip), output block (N, C+1, 128).
In VMEM: batch mean and biased variance by leading-axis loops (f32), std = sqrt(var + 1e-8), channel mean by a sublane reduction.
The concat is written in place: rows 0..C-1 copy x, row C gets the broadcast inject map.
Outside the kernel only reshapes (NCHW <-> (N, C, HW)).
Speed: x is read once and the output written once; all statistics stay in VMEM.

Single pallas_call, 1-D grid over the in_features axis (tk=1024, "arbitrary"). Blocks: x (B, tk), T2 (tk, kd*out_f) bf16, and the output (B, in_f+out_f) bf16 stays resident in VMEM. A (B, kd*out_f) f32 scratch accumulates x@T (MXU, f32 accumulation).
Outside the kernel there are only layout ops: T.transpose(0,2,1).reshape(in_f, kd*out_f). This puts kernel-dim k in lane block k*out_f:(k+1)*out_f, so each k is a lane-dense (B, out_f) slab.
Each step copies its x block into the matching output columns, so the concat happens in-kernel.
On the last step: for each 64-row i-chunk, fori over j accumulates sum_k |M_k[i]-M_k[j]| in f32 registers, then exp and sum. The result minus 1 is written to out[:, in_f:].
Speed: T is read once (memory-bound ~32 MB), and the pairwise part is about 0.5M VPU vreg ops with no HBM intermediates. XLA's version builds the 256x256x128x16 tensor instead.

Two pallas_calls (the stat is a global reduction): both use grid (HW/128,) over pixel strips with block (N, C, 128) f32 = 2 MiB.
Pass 1: batch mean/variance per pixel by leading-axis loops, std = sqrt(var + 1e-8), folded into an f32 (8, 128) VMEM accumulator; last step writes the global mean into an (8,128) output.
Pass 2: copies x into channels 0..C-1 of an (N, C+1, 128) output block and broadcasts the scalar stat into channel C.
Outside the kernels only reshapes.
Speed: two reads of x and one write of the output (the minimum for a global statistic feeding a concat); no intermediate arrays in HBM.

One pallas_call over x viewed as (N, C*HW/128, 128) (here 16 x 32768 x 128), 1-D grid of row blocks (N, 512, 128): 4 MiB per step, 8 MiB double-buffered.
Each step starts an async DMA that copies the VMEM x block straight into the HBM output (pltpu.ANY) at contiguous rows [j*r, j*r+r) of each batch. While it runs, the kernel computes the batch std in f32 over 32-row chunks and adds it into an f32 (32,128) VMEM accumulator.
On the last step it fills a VMEM tile with the global mean of the std and DMAs it into the stat channel rows (C*HW/128 onward).
Only reshapes stay outside the kernel. HBM traffic is 1 read plus 1 write; the previous version did 2 reads plus 1 write, which is where the speedup should come from.

Elementwise and memory-bound. Outside the kernel, reshape only: flatten both inputs to 2D (rows, L), where L is the largest of 1024/512/256/128 that divides the total size; otherwise L is the original last dim.
1D grid over rows, cdiv(rows, 512) steps, blocks of (512, L) or the full rows if fewer. Each f32 block is 2 MiB, so 3 arrays double-buffered come to about 12 MiB.
f32 math in the kernel: abs diff, a select between the quadratic and linear branches, then zero where diff <= threshold. pow(x, 2) is computed as x*x.
The row axis is marked parallel. Lane-dense blocks of 1024 columns keep stores unmasked and DMA near HBM bandwidth. The output is reshaped back to the input shape.

Flatten x to a lane-dense 2D layout (rows, 1024) when the element count is divisible by 1024; otherwise use (rows, W). Outside the kernel this is only a reshape, plus a reshape back afterwards.
The grid is cdiv(rows, 512), with blocks of 512 rows by the full lane width: 2 MiB f32 per block, about 8 MiB VMEM with input and output double-buffered. The axis is marked parallel.
The kernel multiplies by -0.3 in f32 and casts on store. The work is memory-bound, so wide unmasked stores and big blocks keep the per-step overhead small next to the HBM streaming time.

x and y viewed as (B*C*H, W) rows; grid (rows/256,) "arbitrary", blocks (256, W) bf16, each block lies inside one image.
Pooling is linear, so the kernel pools d = x - y (f32): row pairs via stride-2 sublane reads from a VMEM scratch, column pairs via pltpu.roll + add, leaving valid sums on lanes j % 2^k == 0 (columns stay dilated, rows shrink).
Per level the column sums of |window sum| accumulate in an (8, W) f32 scratch; the last step masks the valid lanes, scales by 1/4^k, the mean count and the scale weight, and writes the scalar.
Outside: reshapes, the [0,0] slice and the final bf16 astype.
Speed: one streaming read of x and y (256 MB); the four coarser scales cost under one extra full-size pass of VPU work.

Reshape x (B,C,H,W) -> (B,C,H*W); this is a free layout op. Grid (B, HW//T) with block (1,C,T). T is the largest multiple of 128 that divides HW and keeps the block near 2 MiB (T=4096 for C=128). If HW is not a multiple of 128, T is the full HW.
Inside the kernel, in f32: subtract the max over C (sublane axis), take exp, sum over C, then divide exactly by the sum.
Peak VMEM is about 8 MiB (input and output, each double-buffered); vmem_limit is set to 48 MiB to be safe. Both grid axes are parallel.
The op is memory-bound with one HBM read and one write, which matches XLA's fused softmax. Only the reshapes are outside the kernel.

Grid (B, HW/8192) parallel; x viewed as (B, C, H*W), block (1, C, 8192) bf16; output viewed as (O', B, O, H*W), block (O', 1, O, 8192).
Weight norm (v * g / ||v||) recomputed in-kernel each step in f32 (16x128, negligible), cast to bf16 for one MXU matmul (O,C)@(C,T), f32 acc.
The 5-D bias broadcast is done in-kernel: the (O, T) result is written O' times with a scalar bias from SMEM.
Outside: reshapes and the bias astype to f32 for SMEM. Speed: x read once; the matmul result is reused for all O' output slabs.

Grid (batch, HW/8192), both parallel. x is viewed as (B, C, HW) with block (1, C, 8192) bf16. The output (O_b, B, O, HW) has block (O_b, 1, O, 8192); the weights and gain are full blocks, and the bias sits in SMEM as f32 scalars.
The weight norm and the (O,C)@(C,T) matmul run in the kernel, accumulating in f32. The result is cast to bf16 once.
Speed fix: the previous epilogue re-added the bias in f32 and re-packed to bf16 for every one of the 16 bias rows. Now the bias add is a bf16 add on the already-cast tile, which halves VPU work and skips the repeated f32 to bf16 packing.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes and the bias astype.

Flatten predict to (32768, 1024) (reshape only); grid (64,) over 512-row blocks, 2 MiB f32 per block, sequential ("arbitrary").
Per block: mask = p < thr, loss = where(mask, -log(1 - p + eps), 0); both folded to (8, 1024) f32 VMEM accumulators with leading-axis adds.
Last step reduces both accumulators to scalars and writes loss_sum / mask_sum into a (1, 1) output; reshape to () outside.
Nothing but the reshape is outside the kernel; float32 accumulation throughout.
Speed: single streaming read of the 128 MiB input, no intermediate HBM traffic, cross-lane reduction only once.

Input is flattened to (rows, 1024) lanes. The grid is 1-D over row tiles of up to 1024 rows (4 MiB f32 blocks, 8 MiB double-buffered, vmem limit raised to 48 MiB). That means 32 grid steps instead of 64, which halves the per-step overhead.
Inside each step a fori_loop (unroll=8) walks 8-row slabs. The loss and count accumulators are (8,1024) f32 values carried in registers, so no tile-sized intermediates are written to VMEM.
Each element costs one compare, one sub, one EUP log, two selects and two adds. The negation of the loss is done once at the end instead of per element.
The accumulators are saved to VMEM scratch between grid steps. On the last step the kernel reduces both, divides, and writes a (1,1) result.
Outside the kernel there is only a reshape of the input and a reshape of the output to a scalar.

Flatten x to (M, 256) bf16; grid (M/1024,), x block (1024, 256), weights and biases as resident full blocks.
Both matmuls on the MXU in bf16 with f32 accumulation; bias + relu in f32, hidden cast to bf16 for the second dot.
Outside only reshapes of x, biases and the output.
Speed: fused MLP, the hidden activation never touches HBM; one read of x and one write of y.

Grid of B/8 parallel steps, one group of 8 samples per step. Outside the kernel there are only layout ops: x is reshaped and transposed so each sample row's 64x64 pixels are split into 16 phase blocks (py,px,qy,qx) of 16x16, giving (B*3, 4096) with blocks of (24, 4096). The weights are made block-diagonal across the 8 samples with pad and concatenate, then cast to bf16. fc1's weight is reshaped and transposed into (256, 4*32).
Conv1: for each pool phase q, the 9 taps are built from (24,256) phase blocks using pltpu.roll plus boundary masks. They are stacked into a (256,1024) patch matrix, and one bf16 MXU dot with (256,256) block-diagonal weights gives 8 samples x 32 channels. 2x2 maxpool is an elementwise max over 4 lane blocks. Because tanh is monotonic, the kernel pools first and then applies bias and tanh.
Conv2: 9 accumulated bf16 dots of (128,256) block-diagonal weights x (256,1024) shifted pooled phases, f32 accumulator, then max over 4 phase blocks, bias and tanh. The result is (8*16, 256), rows (sample, channel) and lanes in raster order.
FC: G = h2 @ Wcat in f32 HIGHEST, then a mask, an iota row-selection matmul and a lane-fold matmul reproduce the view(-1,1024) rows. Then tanh, fc2, and a store to the (B*4, 2) output.
Speed idea: the 1 GB conv1 activation never goes to HBM; only the 100 MB input is read, and all matmuls run on the MXU.

Kernel A, grid (N/32,) "parallel", 32 images per step. Conv1 runs as a banded-Toeplitz matmul: 16 output columns × 32 channels per chunk, 120-wide im2col LHS @ (120,1024) weight, accumulated in f32. A max over four 256-lane blocks does pool1. The 2x2 pool output lands in a bf16 VMEM scratch, laid out (row mod 3, row div 3, image, col*32+ch).
Conv2 is a Toeplitz matmul per 12-column chunk: K=3x512, N=384. Pool3 is a max over 3 row-phase matmuls and three 128-lane blocks. Bias and ReLU are applied after the pools, with f32 accumulation throughout.
Kernel B tiles fc1 over K (2304 per step) with a VMEM f32 accumulator. On the last step it applies bias, ReLU and fc2.
Outside the kernels there are only layout ops: strided lax.slice and stack for the conv1 im2col, pad and stack to build the Toeplitz weights, a reshape and transpose to reorder fw1's rows to match the feature layout, a transpose of the features, and bias broadcasting.

Kernel A grid (256/16,) "parallel": block = 64 images as rows (H, 4, 16, 128) bf16; conv1 Toeplitz T1 (640, 3840) and conv2 T2 (1536, 384) resident.
conv1: 2 pooled rows per dot, LHS (256, 640) = 5 input rows lane-concatenated, f32 acc, max over row/col parity, +b, ReLU -> bf16 VMEM map (58, 64, 2048).
conv2: per pooled row one dot (960, 1536) @ (1536, 384) over 5 lane windows, 3x3 max pool as sublane/lane slice maxes, +b, ReLU,
written as features (18, 256, 2560) bf16. Kernel B grid (18,) "arbitrary": (256, 2560) @ (2560, 64) into an f32 scratch, then +b, ReLU, fc2.
Outside: x transpose/pad, Toeplitz weights and fc1 row permutation built with pad/tile/reshape/transpose only (no float math).

One pallas_call, grid (B/8,) over 8-image tiles; input padded to 4 channels and laid out (width-block j, h, b, 32 px x 4 ch) outside (pad/transpose/reshape); all weights resident, vmem_limit 100 MiB.
Each conv+relu+maxpool: per width block, one bf16 MXU matmul (f32 accumulation) of an im2col over 3 kernel rows x [block, first 128 lanes of next block] against a banded Toeplitz weight built outside with pad/broadcast/reshape/slice; columns ordered (parity, pooled px, Cout).
Horizontal pool = max of two aligned lane halves, bias + relu, vertical pool = max over a leading axis after a free reshape; widths halve per stage so the 4 blocks map 1:1 to the next stage.
view(-1, 3136) + Linear: 14 per-row matmuls against fc1 weights re-indexed to (w, c) x (view row, hidden) so the 4 view rows per image come out side by side; relu; block-diagonal fc2 gives a (8, 4*43) block, reshaped to (B*4, 43) outside.
Speed: ~5.7M MXU row pushes (vs ~3x more for per-pixel im2col with 32 channels), no activation goes to HBM; the only HBM traffic is the 50 MB input.

Grid (B/64,) parallel; one fused pallas_call. Outside, boards are re-laid as (B, 8, P) with pixel (h, w) on lane (h+1)*(W+1)+w and zero border rows/column (pad + reshape only), P = 1152 lanes; FC weights get the same zero-padded row layout.
Per board (fori_loop): each 3x3 conv is 9 lane rolls of the (C, P) slab (borders read zeros, no masks), a sublane concat to (9C, P), one bf16 MXU matmul (Cout, 9C) x (9C, P) with f32 acc, bias, ReLU, re-zero of padding lanes.
The 1x1 action/value heads are one (8, 128) matmul; their rows go to a (64*8, P) f32 scratch, and sublane-strided reads give per-channel (64, P) matrices for the FC layers.
FCs: bf16 MXU with f32 acc, log_softmax and the 64->1 dot + tanh in f32. Speed: all activations (GBs in XLA) stay in VMEM; only x and the two outputs touch HBM.

Trunk call, grid (B/8,): x reshaped outside to (B, C, H*W) (one relayout, channels padded to 16) so spatial is lane-dense.
Per 4-image sub-batch (N = 4096 lanes): each 3x3 SAME conv is im2col by 9 lane rolls + edge masks stacked on sublanes
(9C x N bf16), then W (Cout, 9C) @ that with float32 accumulation, bias+relu in float32; conv1->2->3 and both 1x1 heads
stay in VMEM; head rows are scattered into torch's NCHW .view order as (B, 4096) and (B, 2048) float32 outputs.
FC call, grid (B/512, 4096/1024): policy logits accumulate over K into the resident f32 output; the value head
(2048->64 padded to 128, relu, 64->1 lane reduction, tanh) runs at k==0. Log-softmax call, grid (1024/128,): each
block holds all B rows, so the dim-0 max / log-sum-exp is a sublane reduction. Speed: no conv activation touches HBM.

Flatten x to a lane-dense 2D slab (rows, 1024) using reshape, a layout-only op. If the total size isn't divisible by 1024, fall back to (prod(leading dims), last dim).
1D grid over rows with blocks of up to 512x1024 f32 (2 MiB). Input plus output, double-buffered, comes to about 8 MiB of VMEM, under the 16 MiB default. The grid uses cdiv, so a partial last block is fine for elementwise work.
The kernel computes round(x*255), clips to [0,255] and divides by 255 in f32. No accumulator is needed.
Outside the kernel there are only the reshapes. The dimension is marked parallel. The op is memory-bound, so the speed comes from large lane-dense blocks that run near HBM bandwidth.

Reshape audio (B, L) to (B, L/128, 128); grid (B,), one whole row per step as a (1, 2048, 128) f32 block (1 MiB).
Row max/min: elementwise max/min over the leading (rows/8) vreg groups, then one small cross-sublane/lane reduce.
Normalize in the same step with a single reciprocal per row: (x - min) * inv * 2 - 1.
Outside only reshapes. Speed: one read and one write of the input, versus XLA's two reads.

x flattened to (rows, 1024) lanes; grid over rows with (1024, 1024) bf16 blocks (2 MiB).
w1, w2 passed as f32 scalars in SMEM; elementwise max/min/scale in f32, cast to bf16 on store.
Outside the kernel: reshape and astype of the two scalars only.
Speed: pure streaming kernel, wide lane-dense blocks, one read and one write of x.

x viewed as (N*C*H, W) bf16 (free reshape); 1-D grid over blocks of 32 planes: in (32*H, W) = 4 MiB, out (32*Ho, Wo).
in-kernel fori_loop over 4-plane chunks: cast to f32 into a VMEM scratch, 4 sublane-strided loads (stride 4) + max = H pooling.
W pooling: one bf16 MXU matmul with an iota-built 0/1 matrix gathers the 4 lane phases into 128-aligned column groups
(exact: one nonzero per column, f32 accumulation), then max over the 4 groups; result stored as bf16.
outside the kernel only reshapes (replicate pad / VALID crop are layout ops and are no-ops for this config).
speed: x is streamed from HBM exactly once and the 16x smaller output written once; all pooling work stays in VMEM.

Reshape x, y to (N, C, H*W); grid (N, HW/2048) with (1, C, 2048) f32 blocks (1 MiB each).
a and b passed as (C, 1) resident blocks, broadcast along lanes in-kernel; f32 math, no accumulator.
Only reshapes outside; the resize branch is skipped because shapes match.
Speed: memory bound, two reads and one write per element, lane-dense blocks.

Flatten pred/target to lane-dense (R, L), with L=1024 when the size divides evenly, else the last dim. Grid is (R//bm,) with bm up to 1024 rows, so each input block is 2 MiB bf16 and about 8 MiB is double-buffered.
Each step runs a fori_loop over 32-row chunks: upcast to f32, compute e=t-p, loss=max(3e,4e), and sum into an (8,L) f32 running value that is added to a VMEM scratch accumulator.
On the last step the kernel reduces the scratch to one value and multiplies by d1/total, because sum over dim1 then mean over the rest equals total_sum/(B*d2*d3).
Outside the kernel there is only reshape (plus a zero pad in the fallback) and astype to bf16. The quantile 4.0 is hard-coded because CONFIG can't be read.
Each input is read once, so the kernel should run at HBM bandwidth, the limit for this reduction.

Reshape x (B,C,H,W) to (B,C,H*W); this is a layout-only op. Grid is (B, cdiv(HW, T)) and both axes are parallel. Each block is (1, C, T), with T a multiple of 128 sized so one block is about 2 MiB (T=4096 for C=128). With input and output double-buffered that is about 8 MiB of VMEM.
Inside the kernel, the sum of squares over channels (the sublane axis) is computed in f32. The kernel then multiplies by rsqrt(mean + eps) and stores the result in x's dtype.
The only ops outside the kernel are the two reshapes. The kernel is memory-bound, so the aim is to read and write x once each in large, lane-dense tiles.

Call 1: softmax of W over O. Grid over i in chunks of 16; block (O, 16, J) f32, sublane-strided loads pull each (O, J) slab,
softmax over sublanes, written bf16 as columns of Wt (O, I*J) so the second call contracts (i, j) on the MXU directly.
Call 2: grid (rows/1024, I/8), I-chunk axis sequential. x1, x2 tiles are transposed once into VMEM ((I, tm), (J, tm)); per step the
outer products U[(i,j), m] = x1[m,i]*x2[m,j] for 8 values of i (sublane broadcast, f32 mul, bf16) feed acc(O, tm) += Wt_chunk @ U
(f32 acc). Last step: L1-normalise over O (sublane sum) and transpose back to (tm, O). Outside: only reshapes.
Speed: never materialises XLA's (rows, O, J) 2 GB intermediate; 275 GFLOP on the MXU plus one VPU multiply per product.

x is reshaped (free layout op) to (B, C, D, H*W). Two pallas_calls, both on grid (B, D), x block (1, C, 1, H*W) bf16 (1 MiB).
K1: per-(c,w) and per-(c,h) sums come from the MXU, multiplying the x tile by in-kernel one-hot matrices (H*W,W) and (H*W,H) that are built once into scratch. Sums accumulate in f32 in output blocks that stay resident across d. Per-(c,d) sums are a lane-sum dropped into column d.
K2: at d==0 per batch, the first 1x1x1 conv is applied to the three means (f32 split into hi+lo bf16 for accuracy). The result is spread to base (Cr,H*W) = pw expanded over w + ph expanded over h, via one-hot matmuls, and kept in VMEM scratch. Each d step: h = relu(base + pd[:,d] + b1) in bf16; g = W2^T @ h with f32 accumulation; sigmoid computed as 0.5*tanh(0.5g)+0.5; out = x*g, worked in 1024-lane chunks.
Outside the kernels: only reshape, transpose of the weights, and astype of the biases. The work is memory bound: x is read twice and written once.

Flatten x from (B,C,H,W) to (B*C, H*W) with a reshape. Expand lam to one value per row, shape (B*C,1), using only broadcast and reshape.
Grid is (rows/br, cols/bc). Blocks are about (256, 4096) bf16, which is 2 MiB each, so input plus output with double buffering is about 8 MiB of VMEM. Both grid axes are marked parallel.
Inside the kernel: t = bf16(lam*sigma^2/L), then out = where(|x|>t, x - sign(x)*t, 0). The math runs in f32 and is cast to bf16 on store. Each element has a single rounding, so the result should match the bf16 reference.
Outside the kernel there are only reshape and broadcast steps. The kernel is memory bound, and the large lane-dense blocks are meant to reach close to HBM bandwidth.

Grid (batch, H/64); blocks (C, 64, W=256) f32 of x plus 8-row halo blocks above/below (index maps clamp at the edges, rows zeroed).
Each step recomputes the spectral-norm power iteration exactly in f32 on the VPU (W is only 128x1152) and gets 1/sigma.
Sublane-strided loads re-lay the 66 input rows as a row-major (row, channel) bf16 scratch; per output row one MXU matmul
Wbig (3Co [kw], 3Ci [kh]) @ (3Ci, 256) with f32 acc, kw taps as lane rolls with edge masks; * 1/sigma + bias, LeakyReLU(0.2),
+ the exact f32 residual, strided store back to NCHW. Outside: weight transpose/reshape/cast only.
Speed: one bf16 pass on the MXU vs the reference's HIGHEST-precision conv; x read ~1.25x and written once.

Grid (B, C/64); x reshaped to (B, C, H*W), block (1, 64, H*W) f32 (4 MiB); w block (64, N); out block (1, 1, N) resident over C.
f32 throughout: lane-sum gives the pooled (64, 1) column, then sum(pooled * w_tile, axis=0) adds a (1, N) partial to the output.
Bias initializes the output at the first C step; outside only reshapes.
Speed idea: the 268 MB x read dominates; the tiny GEMV is done on the VPU so no transpose or MXU padding is needed.

Three pallas_calls (InstanceNorm needs whole-image stats): conv1+stats, IN1+relu+conv2+stats, IN2+residual+relu.
Conv passes: grid (N, H/32), image axis parallel, rows arbitrary; blocks (1, C, 32, W) f32 in native NCHW plus two 8-row
halo blocks (index maps clamp at the edges, rows masked to zero there); vmem limit 96 MiB. Rows are gathered with stride
sublane loads, pre-activated (pass 2 applies relu(IN1) from the accumulated stats), and each row's 3 lane-shifted copies are
split into bf16 hi/lo taps; 4-row groups are Whi@Phi + Wlo@Phi + Whi@Plo per kernel row (bf16x3, f32 acc; one bf16 pass
