would give ~1e-2 error after the two normalizations). Per-channel sum / sum^2 accumulate as (C, 128) lane partials in a
resident output block. Final pass: relu(x + y2*a + b) by strided rows. Speed: ~0.93 TFLOP of MXU vs the 6-pass HIGHEST ref.

Single pallas_call, grid=(1,), seq passed via scalar prefetch (SMEM); logprobs is reshaped (free) to (N*V/128, 128) and left in HBM (pl.ANY).
DMA gather: for every flattened row r it copies one 128-lane strip, logprobs[r, seq_r//128*128 : +128], into a VMEM buffer of shape (2, 2048, 128). Chunks of 2048 rows are double-buffered: the next chunk's DMAs are issued before the current chunk is waited on, with one wait per chunk on a shared semaphore. So about 8 MB is read instead of 256 MB.
Select: each (128,128) strip block is transposed, then iota(sublane) == seq%128 picks the wanted element and a sublane sum gives a lane-dense (1,128) row. This lines up with reward and mask in their (rows/128, 128) layout.
Mask: seq_prev = concat(ones, seq[:, :-1]) is built outside the kernel with layout ops only; mask = seq_prev > 0 and the f32 (1,128) numerator/denominator accumulation happen in the kernel, and the final divide is written to a (1,1) output.
Outside the kernel there is only reshape, concatenate, slice and zero padding to a multiple of 2048 rows (padded rows have mask 0).

Grid (N/256,) "arbitrary": logprobs as the (N, V) bitcast view, blocks (256, 4096) f32 (4 MB); seq, prev-token and reward as (256, 1)
columns. Per 8-row chunk: lane-iota == seq selects the gathered value, lane sum gives it per row; -g*reward*mask and mask summed in
f32, accumulated in (1,1) scratch; numerator/denominator divided at the last step. Outside: reshapes and the shifted-seq concatenate.
Speed idea: one streaming HBM pass like XLA instead of attempt 1's 16384 tiny DMAs, whose scalar issue loop was the bottleneck.

Reshape (2,B,C,H,W) -> (2, R, L) with L=1024 (or 128) lanes; grid (2 pairs, R/tb) both arbitrary, blocks (1, tb<=1024, L) bf16 (~2 MiB each, ~8 MiB double-buffered for 2 inputs).
Kernel upcasts to f32; pair 0 accumulates (sigmoid(p)-l)^2 (sigmoid via tanh, 1 EUP op), pair 1 accumulates max(x,0)-x*y+log1p(exp(-|x|)).
Per-tile reduction to (8, L) via leading-axis adds into a (2,8,L) f32 VMEM scratch; no cross-lane work in the hot loop.
On the last grid step: full reduce, 2*sqrt(s0/N+smooth)+s1/N written to a resident (1,1) f32 output.
Outside: only reshape and astype to the input dtype. Memory-bound single pass over 128 MB.

inputs viewed as (B*C, H, S) (leading-dim merge only); grid (B*C//bc,) "arbitrary", blocks (bc, H, S) ~2 MiB per input.
in-kernel nested fori_loop over (bc, H/16) chunks of (16, S) rows: zero-mean, then the three centered lane-reduced sums (xt, tt, res^2) in float32.
per-row loss = 10*log10(alpha^2*Stt/(Sres+eps)+eps) (sum((alpha*t)^2) == alpha^2*Stt); losses summed into a (16,1) f32 VMEM accumulator.
the last grid step writes -(total)/rows into a (1,1) output; only a reshape to () stays outside. Speed: one HBM pass over both inputs.

Flatten x (layout-only reshape) to a lane-dense 2D slab (rows, L), where L is 1024/512/256/128, whichever divides the size first; if none does, fall back to the last dimension.
1D grid over rows with blocks of (512, L) f32, at most 2 MiB per block. Input and output, each double-buffered, come to about 8 MiB of VMEM. Grid axis is parallel.
Inside the kernel, all f32: min(x, 50), log1p(exp()), then erf from XLA's f32 rational approximation (clamp to [-4,4], odd polynomial divided by an even one), then multiply by x.
Only the reshape happens outside the kernel. The op is memory-bound with a single pass over HBM; the exp, log and divide run on the EUP and overlap with the DMA.

x reshaped (layout only) to (B, C, S); grid (B, S/8192) both parallel, block (1, C, 8192) = 4 MiB f32.
weight and bias reshaped to (C, 1) columns, same block every step (fetched once), lane-broadcast in-kernel.
In-kernel: x * w + b in f32; no accumulator. Outside: reshapes only.
Speed: memory-bound streaming at one read + one write of x with large blocks to amortize per-step overhead.

Flatten x to (B, C, S) with S = prod(spatial). Grid (B, S//t), with t=4096 when it divides S and t=S otherwise; x and out blocks are (1, C, t).
weight and bias are broadcast to (C, t) outside the kernel (a layout op). Their block index is constant, so each is DMA'd once and stays in VMEM.
The kernel is a pure elementwise multiply-add in f32 with no lane broadcast, so it should be HBM-bound like XLA.
VMEM use: 4 arrays x 2 MiB x 2 buffers = 16 MiB, so the limit is raised to 48 MiB. Only reshape and broadcast_to run outside the kernel.

Reshape x (B,C,H,W) -> (B*C, H*W) so every row is one (batch, channel) plane, and broadcast/reshape weight and bias to (B*C, 1). These are layout ops only.
Grid is (rows/tr, cols/tw) with tr up to 256 (multiple of 8) and tw up to 2048 (multiple of 128). If no such divisor exists, the full dim is used. Both axes are parallel, and the column axis is innermost so the (tr,1) weight/bias blocks stay resident.
The kernel computes o = x*w + b in f32 and casts on store. Each step uses 2 MiB per tile, about 8 MiB total with in/out double buffering, which is well under 16 MiB.
Speed: one HBM read and one HBM write with wide lane-dense tiles; this should match XLA's fused elementwise bandwidth.

Flatten all three inputs (layout only) to (R, 1024) f32, padding with zeros only when the size is not a multiple of the block. Zero padding adds nothing, because the padded mask is 0.
Grid is (R/bm,) with bm up to 1024 rows, so each block is 4 MiB per input. The axis is 'arbitrary' (a sequential reduction), and vmem_limit is raised to 64 MiB to cover 3 inputs x 2 buffers.
Each step folds clip(p-n+margin)*m and m into two (8,1024) f32 VMEM accumulators using plain vector adds, with no cross-lane work per step.
On the last step it reduces both accumulators to scalars, computes weight*s/max(cnt,1), and writes the result to an (8,128) output. Outside the kernel, the only step is slicing out [0,0].
It reads the inputs exactly once, so speed is limited only by HBM bandwidth.

grid (N, cdiv(H_out,R)+1), R=16 rows; axis 1 sequential: step s DMAs input row-block s (1,C,R,W) bf16 into a
3-slot bf16 VMEM ring (blocks b-1, b, b+1; no copies) and emits output block b=s-1 (1,O,R,W_out) bf16.
depthwise: vertical taps on the MXU per channel, Vc (K*R, 3R) banded bf16 @ window (3R, W) -> f32 P_j rows
(Vc is laid out from the weights with pad/reshape/slice only); horizontal taps = pltpu.roll + edge masks + bias.
pointwise 1x1 on the MXU per output row: sublane-strided loads gather the (C,W) slab -> bf16 dot pw (O,C),
f32 accumulate, + bias, strided store, then cast to bf16. x read once, output written once, no transposes.

grid (B, cdiv(Hout, 32)); per step an x block (C, 32, W) f32 in native NCHW layout plus an 8-row halo block (C, 8, W) of the following rows.
depthwise KxK on the VPU per channel (fori over C): sublane-offset row loads for kh, lane rolls for kw, SMEM scalar weights, f32 math.
the depthwise result goes to VMEM scratch (C*32, 128) x2 lane halves; a sublane-strided load (stride 32) gathers one output row for all channels -> (C, W).
pointwise 1x1 = MXU dot pw(O,C) bf16 @ (C,W) bf16 with f32 accumulation, scattered back by a strided store into (O*32, 128) scratch.
copy-out adds the bias (SMEM scalar) and writes NCHW directly (masked W tail); outside the kernel only weight reshapes.

no grid; x and the output stay in HBM (memory_space=ANY), the whole op is DMA traffic.
x (L, N, E) is copied HBM->HBM into out[0:L] as ~8 concurrent leading-dim chunk DMAs.
the bias row is broadcast to (1, N, E) in a VMEM scratch inside the kernel and DMA'd to out[L].
no float math, no accumulator; outside only bias.reshape(1, E). Speed: pure DMA at HBM bandwidth.

Grid (N,) with the whole NCHW image (1, 3, 512, 512) f32 as one block; a fori_loop over the 64 pooled rows (8 conv rows each); a (3, 528, 512) padded VMEM copy keeps every 24-row window load aligned.
Per pooled row: 9 lane-shifted (24, 512) windows (3 channels x 3 dx) are stacked into a (256, 512) bf16 tap matrix; a layout-built weight wbig (128, 256) (rows (o, r), cols (c, dx, q), dy encoded by q - r) gives all 16 channels x 8 conv rows in one MXU matmul with f32 accumulation; bias + ReLU in f32.
Pooling and the Linear are matmuls too: a 0/1 (16, 128) matrix sums the 8 rows, a (512, 128) matrix built from fc_w by repeat/pad sums 8-column groups and applies fc_w per 16-column chunk; scale 1/64 and bias in f32. Single-pass bf16 is ~1e-4 abs on outputs ~0.03.
Outside: layout-only weight prep and the final (N, 16, 64, 16) -> (131072, 4) reshape (2 MB); the per-row results are moved to (c, i) order in-kernel with stride-16 sublane loads.
Speed: x (100 MB) read once, the 134M-element conv activation never leaves VMEM; XLA runs a HIGHEST-precision 3-channel conv plus NCHW transposes.

grid (N, cdiv(OH,T)), T=16 output rows per step; input block (C,T,W) native NCHW, output block (O,T,OW) native NCHW.
in-kernel (c,h)->(h,c) via a (C*T,128) VMEM copy + sublane-strided loads; each input row -> (C,Wp) f32, KW lane-rolled copies stored bf16
in a window buffer (T+KH-1, KW*C, Wp); the KH-1 halo rows are carried across steps (row axis "arbitrary"), so no halo re-reads.
per output row one MXU matmul (O, KH*KW*C) bf16 @ (KH*KW*C, Wp) bf16 -> f32 accumulate, ReLU, sublane-strided store into (O*T,128) chunks.
outside only filter transpose/slice/concat/reshape/astype (tiny); speed: no HBM transposes, K=2048 single-pass bf16 matmuls.

Grid (D0, D1/32); x blocks (1, 32, D2, 128) bf16 = 4096 rows over the native layout, merged in-kernel (leading dims).
Hidden sizes 50/100 are zero-padded to 128 outside (pad + astype on weights only), exact under relu.
In-kernel: two bf16 matmuls with float32 accumulation, then the 1-unit head as a float32 lane reduction giving the
(rows, 1) column, stored per D1 slab into the (1, 32, D2, 1) output block.
Speed: memory-bound single pass; the whole MLP is fused.

x (free reshape) -> (131072, 128) bf16 rows; grid over 256-row blocks; output written directly in its final (524288, 32, 32) layout, blocks (1024, 32, 32).
Per block: f32 transpose on the XLU puts 128 consecutive elements on sublanes; per 128-column chunk one MXU matmul with
K1 = placement of w1 (128, 128*32) turns each element column into 32 hidden lanes (outer product x*w1), + b1, relu.
Second layer: per 128-lane hidden slab (4 elements) one matmul with w2 spread so each element's 32 outputs start a fresh
128-lane tile; aligned (128, 32) slices are reshaped to (4, 32, 32) and stored. f32 accumulation, bf16 operands.
Outside: K1/W2 built by pad+concatenate, biases tiled, casts. Speed: bound by the (32,32)-tiled 1 GB output write; MXU work hides under it.

x (B, C, bins, W) reshaped to (B, C*bins, W); grid (C*bins/256 rows "parallel", B/2 "arbitrary"), block (2, 256, W).
Sum over batch accumulates in a float32 VMEM scratch (256, W), stored as bf16 on the last batch step.
Outside the kernel: reshapes, and the bin centers tiled to a (256, 1) f32 column (row r uses center r % bins).
Sigmoids computed in f32; when delta/2 == 0 the two sigmoids are identical, so one is computed and reused.
Memory-bound: one pass over x (64 MB), lane-dense W=1024 blocks.

grid (B, HW//TS) over x/target viewed as (B, C, HW); blocks (1, C, TS) f32 with TS=4096 (2 MiB per input, 8 MiB double-buffered).
a fori_loop walks 512-lane chunks: log-softmax over C (sublanes) as lse = max + log(sum exp(x - max)), then per position
sum_c[xlogy(t,t) - t*x] + lse * sum_c t  (== sum_c of the reference's pointwise term), all in f32.
per-position sums accumulate in a (1, CH) f32 VMEM scratch over the whole grid ("arbitrary"); the last step reduces to a scalar
and scales by 1/(B*C*HW). Outside: only reshapes. Speed: single fused pass over 256 MiB, memory-bound.

Reshape inputs (B,C,H,W)->(B,C,H*W) (layout only). Grid (B, HW/T), both parallel; blocks (1,C,T) with T = largest multiple of 128 <= 2048 dividing HW (else full HW).
Kernel: cast bf16->f32, e=exp(m+0.5v), lv=e*e*(exp(v)-1), s=sum over C (sublane axis)+eps in f32, inv=1/s; outputs e*inv and lv*inv*inv cast to bf16.
Only reshapes outside the kernel. Single memory-bound pass: read 2 inputs and write 2 outputs once; ~512 KiB bf16 blocks keep VMEM small; vmem limit raised to 64 MiB for safety.

Two pallas_calls on z viewed as (S*B, D) (leading-dim merge, free). Call 1, grid (S/128,): LayerNorm of the z2 half in f32 on (128*B, Dh) blocks, then 16 sublane-strided VMEM reads write it batch-major as zn_t (B, S, Dh) bf16, so S lands on sublanes for the MXU.
Call 2, grid (S/256, B) with B sequential: (256, S) x (S, Dh) bf16 MXU matmul (W is bf16-exact, f32 acc) + bias, written with a static strided store (one pl.when per b) into an interleaved (256*B, Dh) f32 scratch.
After the last b the scratch is multiplied by the z1 block (read in its native layout) and stored once.
Outside only reshapes and the [:S] slices. Speed: no XLA transposes; z1 and the output keep their native layout.

Reshape the NCHW inputs to (B, C, H*W) so H*W is the lane dimension. The grid is (B, HW//T), with both axes "parallel".
The block size is (1, C, T). T is the largest multiple of 128 that divides H*W while keeping one block at or under about 2 MiB. Three arrays, double-buffered, come to roughly 12 MiB or less.
Inside the kernel, the 1x1 conv is a dot of the (G, C) weight with the (C, T) tile, accumulated in f32 at HIGHEST precision. The kernel adds the bias, applies tanh, clamps at 0, multiplies each group's C/G data channels by that group's gate row, and stores the result.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes and a transpose of the weight to (G, C) and the bias to (G, 1).
The task is memory-bound: the kernel reads the data and gate inputs once and writes the output once, and avoids XLA's extra round trip of the gate through memory.

grid (batch, row-blocks): x block (1, TL=1024, C) bf16, out block (1, TL/2, C); C full width (lane dense).
in-kernel fori_loop over 256-row chunks: square in float32, stash in a (256, C) f32 VMEM scratch, then the pair sum = two stride-2 sublane loads (even/odd rows).
out = (2/k) * sum of the k squared rows (k=2 -> a^2 + b^2), cast to the input dtype on store.
nothing outside the kernel; speed: single HBM read of x and write of the half-length output, no relayout copies.

Grid (N,) parallel; one whole image per step: x block (1, C, H, W) bf16 in native NCHW, out block (1, Co, 125, 125) bf16;
vmem limit 100 MiB (double buffers + f32 row scratch + 16 MiB bf16 tap scratch + f32 output staging).
Weight standardization (mean/var over ci,kh,kw per co) runs in-kernel in f32 each step, rounded once to bf16 for the MXU.
bf16 rows are gathered as uint32 pairs (stride-H/2 sublane loads, unpacked with shifts/bitcasts) into a row-major f32
scratch; P[r] stacks the 4 left-rolled copies (VALID conv: wrapped lanes only hit dropped columns) as (4C, W) bf16, and each
5-row output group is sum_kh Ws[kh] (Co, 4C) @ (4C, 5W) with f32 acc + bias. Rows go to an f32 (Co, 128, W) staging
buffer by strided stores, then one cast/store of the (Co, 125, 125) block. Speed: 131 GFLOP single-pass MXU, one HBM pass.

Grid (N,) parallel, one NCHW image (1, C, H, W) bf16 per step; output block (1, Co, Ho, Wo) written NCHW directly; 100 MB VMEM limit.
Weights standardized in f32 in-kernel and stored as one (k*Co, k*C) bf16 LHS: rows (kh, co), columns (kw, ci).
x is unpacked to row-major (H, C, W) f32 with stride-H/2 u32 loads, then each row becomes 4 lane-rolled (kw) bf16 copies: patches (H, k*C, W).
Per 4 patch rows: one (512, 512) @ (512, 4W) matmul, f32 accumulation, computes all 4 kernel rows at once (each patch tile latched once, 512 streamed rows); output row o += Y_kh[o + kh] in an f32 VMEM accumulator.
Bias added while staging rows back to channel-major with strided stores; final slice to (Ho, Wo) and bf16 cast.

Grid (B*C/P,) over whole (H, W) planes of the native layout viewed as (B*C, H, W); block (P, 512, 512) f32 with P = 4 (4 MB).
Per plane a fori_loop walks aligned 8-row chunks: vertical neighbour via sublane roll of the chunk plus the previous chunk's last row (carried), horizontal neighbour via a lane roll; wrap row/column are masked. |diff| sums go into two (8, W) f32 carries and VMEM accumulators.
Last grid step reduces both to scalars and applies (h_tv/count_h + w_tv/count_w)/b with the counts taken from the shape.
Outside the kernel: leading-dim reshape, (1,1)->() reshape.
Speed: x (256 MB) read once; XLA materializes or re-reads shifted slices for the two differences.

grid (A, Bt/nb), nb=32 (a,b) pairs per step; blocks E (nb,M,Hd), Tt (nb,K,J), T (nb,J,N), out (nb,M,N), w (Hd,K) resident.
outside the kernel only jnp.transpose(topic_emb) (the reference's own full transpose, a layout op).
per pair (fori, unroll 4): tsw = w@X, S = E@tsw, softmax over the M rows in f32, H = P@T; all dots bf16 in / f32 accumulate.
speed: one HBM pass over E (the big operand) and the outputs; intermediates never leave VMEM/vregs.

The reference returns x unchanged; its TV loss is never returned, so XLA eliminates it and there is nothing to compute.
No grid: input and output stay in HBM (memory_space=ANY) and one async DMA copies x to the output, then waits.
No accumulator; nothing outside the kernel.
Speed idea: a single full-bandwidth HBM->HBM DMA with no VMEM staging; the reference can forward its input for free, so this may still lose on speed.

No grid. Input and output both stay in HBM (memory_space=pl.ANY), so nothing is staged in VMEM and there is no accumulator.
The kernel splits the copy along the leading axis into up to 8 HBM->HBM DMAs, starts them all, then waits on each one, so several are in flight together.
Nothing runs outside the kernel. The reference's TV loss is dead code in XLA, so returning x is the only observable work.
Speed idea: concurrent DMAs get closer to peak HBM bandwidth than one large DMA. This is still a 64 MiB read plus a 64 MiB write, and the reference is a zero-copy forward, so passing 0.7x is probably impossible for any valid kernel.

Outside (layout ops only): pad + space-to-depth x into (B, 65, 72, 256) 8x8 blocks, so conv1 (8x8, stride 4) becomes a
2x2 stride-1 conv whose 128 output lanes are the 2x2 phases of conv1 = conv2's space-to-depth input; weights are
re-laid out with pad/stack/transpose. Kernel A, grid (B,): conv1 -> conv2 -> conv3 -> 2x2 max-pool fused in VMEM;
im2col by sublane roll+mask and 128-aligned lane concat, 8-row chunks of bf16 MXU matmuls with f32 accumulation,
conv3 packs two 64-ch taps per 128 lanes, pool via stride-2 loads, then transposed to (64, 1024) = NCHW flatten.
Kernel B: fc1 K-tiled (tk=4096) with a (B, 512) f32 VMEM accumulator, relu and fc2 fused on the last step.

Reshape z (B,C,H,W) to (B,C,HW) (layout op only) and use grid (B, HW//tn) with tn=512. The z block is (1,C,tn); the full codebook (n_e,C) and its transpose (C,n_e) stay resident in VMEM.
In-kernel distances: d = (||z||^2 + ||e||^2) - 2*cb@z_blk, giving (n_e,tn) in f32. The matmul uses a bf16x3 split (hi/lo, f32 accumulation), which is close to f32 accuracy so argmin should match the HIGHEST-precision reference.
Argmin runs over the sublane axis: a min, then a masked min over a float iota so ties go to the first index. The gather is a matmul of cbT (hi+lo bf16) with an exact bf16 one-hot.
Outputs: z_q (1,C,tn) blocks written straight back in NCHW, idx (1,1,tn) int32, and the loss summed into a resident (1,1) output across an 'arbitrary' grid and scaled by (1+beta)/N on the last step.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes, one transpose of the codebook, and the final reshape of loss to a scalar.

Layer 0 (Cin=3): im2col via layout-only pad/slice/concat to K=32, then grid (B, H/16) matmul (16*W, 32) @ (32, 64) + bias + ReLU.
Layers 1-12: one pallas_call each, NHWC, grid (B, H/8); main block (1, 8, W, Cin) plus two 1-row halo blocks (zeroed at the image edge) assembled into a (10, W, Cin) VMEM window; 3 matmuls (8W, Cin) @ (Cin, 3*Cout) with the kw taps stacked in N, f32 accumulation, kw=0/2 results shifted one row with pltpu.roll and masked at W edges, + bias, ReLU.
Max-pool layers (1, 3, 6) are fused: h-pair max on a leading axis, w-pair max via roll, even rows taken with a strided VMEM read; output written at half resolution.
Outside: NCHW<->NHWC transposes, weight transposes/reshapes, layer-0 im2col (layout only). bf16 activations between layers, vmem limit 64 MiB for the 512-channel weights.
Speed: no padded copies of activations in HBM, every matmul operand aligned, pools never materialize the full-resolution output.

Flatten both bf16 inputs to (rows, L) with L=512 lanes when possible; grid over row blocks of up to 2048 rows (2 MiB per input block, ~8 MiB double-buffered), single 'arbitrary' axis.
Inside: fori_loop over 64-row chunks, upcast to f32, e=y-yp, f=e*tanh(e/2) (algebraically equal to 2e/(1+exp(-e))-e, one EUP op), fold chunk into an (8,L) f32 VMEM accumulator with VPU adds only.
Last step: full reduce acc, divide by element count, write (1,1) f32 output.
Outside: only reshape of inputs, reshape of (1,1)->() and astype to the input dtype.
Speed: one pass over 134 MB at HBM bandwidth, no intermediate arrays in HBM.

Grid (B,) 'parallel'; one block (1, C, H, W) bf16 per sample in native layout (8 MiB), vmem limit raised for double buffering.
Pass 1 (fori over channels): per-channel mean and centred sum of squares in f32 into (C, 128) VMEM scratch.
Layer mean/var come from the channel stats exactly (sum ss_c + n*sum (m_c - M)^2), unbiased (ddof=1); rho, gamma, beta fold into per-channel scale a_c and shift b_c.
Pass 2 (fori over channels): out = x*a_c + b_c in f32, rounded once to bf16. Outside: only reshapes/astype of the (B, C) gamma/beta and rho.
Speed: x read from HBM once, written once (2 passes over VMEM), instead of XLA's separate mean/var/normalise passes.

Grid (B*C, H/tr) over the native layout viewed as (B*C, H, W); block (1, tr, 256) f32 with tr sized to 2 MB.
Each step runs a fori_loop over 8-row slices computing softplus(-x) = max(-x,0) + log1p(exp(-|x|)) (same value as the reference's stable form, one exp instead of two) into an (8, W) f32 carry, then into an (8, W) VMEM accumulator.
Last step reduces to (1,1) and multiplies by 1/N.
Outside the kernel: leading-dim reshape, (1,1)->() reshape.
Speed: single memory-bound pass over 256 MB with 2 transcendental ops per element.

Grid (batch, H/32), chunk axis sequential: each step pools a (1, C, 32, 256) f32 chunk (sublane-strided row-pair loads, vertical sum in
f32, horizontal pair-sum and /4 as an MXU matmul with a hi/lo bf16 split) into a row-major (row, channel) bf16 scratch with zero pad rows.
Last chunk: conv1 (4x4, pad 1 -> 127) and conv2 (-> 126) per output row as Wbig (4Co [kw], 4Ci [kh]) @ (4Ci, 128) on the MXU (f32 acc),
kw taps as lane rolls with edge masks, + bias, LeakyReLU(0.1); conv1 rows go to a second bf16 scratch (col/row 127 zeroed as padding),
conv2 rows are strided-stored into a (C, 128, 128) f32 output block. Outside: weight transpose/cast and the final [:126, :126] slice.
Speed: single bf16 MXU pass vs the HIGHEST-precision reference convs; x read once, pooled/conv1 maps stay in VMEM.

One generic pallas_call per 3x3/7x7 conv (39 calls): NHWC bf16 activations, grid (N, H/32) "parallel", main row block (1,32,W,C) plus p one-row halo blocks above and below (clamped, zeroed outside the image) copied into a zero-bordered f32 VMEM scratch.
Row chunks of ~1024 pixels: column-shifted slices concatenated into K = k*C lanes when C % 128 == 0 (else per-tap dots), k bf16 MXU dots with f32 accumulation, bias + ReLU in f32; 2x2 max pools fused (row pairs via leading split, column pairs via stride-2 sublane reads from a scratch).
1x1 layers fused: conv1_1 is a "pre" matmul over a 27-channel im2col of the raw input (built outside with pad/slice/concat), conv6_1/conv6_2 and Mconv6/Mconv7 are "post" matmuls on the conv5_3 / Mconv5 tiles; 22-part heads zero-padded to 128 lanes, stage input reordered to [out1_0, out_pad] with Mconv1 weights permuted/padded to match (layout ops only).
Speed: single-pass bf16 MXU instead of the reference's 6-pass f32 HIGHEST convs; deep K contractions; no 1x1 activations or pooled pre-images touch HBM.

x viewed as (B, C, H*W); grid (B, HW/2048); block (1, 512, 2048) bf16; output (B, 1, C) block resident across the spatial axis.
f32 accumulator (C, 128): each step adds the 16 lane-aligned 128-wide slices of the block (VPU only).
Last spatial step: one lane reduce to (C,1), divide by HW, L2-normalize over C, turn the column into a (1,C) row with an iota-eye select + sublane sum, store.
Outside: only reshapes.
Speed: single pass over the 268 MB input, memory-bound, cross-lane work once per batch row.

Grid (B, HW/tl), tl<=4096; x viewed as (B, C, HW) with block (1, C, tl) bf16 (4 MiB, 8 MiB double-buffered).
Reduction runs on the MXU: x_blk (C, tl) @ ones (tl, 128) bf16 -> f32, accumulated into a (C, 128) f32 VMEM scratch. The ones scratch is filled at j==0.
Last step: transpose the acc, take row 0 as (1, C), divide by HW, L2-normalize, store a lane-dense (1, 1, C) output block.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes. Speed idea: moving the reduction from the VPU to the MXU makes the kernel HBM-bound, and the larger block halves the step count.

Grid (N, HW/2048): N parallel, HW tiles arbitrary; x viewed as (N, C, H*W) (free reshape), block (1, C, 2048) f32.
f32 accumulator scratch (C, 128): each step adds the 16 lane chunks of the tile with plain VPU adds (no per-step lane reduce).
Last HW step: one lane reduction to (C, 1), mean, L2 norm over channels, write (1, C, 1); outside only the reshape to (N, C).
Speed: single streaming pass over x at HBM bandwidth.

Grid (N, HW//tk), tk up to 4096 lanes; each input block is (1, C, tk) f32, 8 MiB when tk is 4096, and double buffering stays inside a 48 MiB VMEM limit.
The kernel walks the block in 8-row chunks with fori_loop. Each chunk's 128-lane slices are summed pairwise in registers, then added once into an f32 (C, 128) VMEM accumulator. This avoids the 64-vreg intermediates of the previous version, which spilled to VMEM.
On the last HW step the kernel sums the accumulator's lanes, multiplies by 1/HW, and L2-normalizes over C, all in f32 inside the kernel.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes: (N,C,H,W) to (N,C,HW), and the (N,C,1) output to (N,C). The kernel is memory-bound, so the goal is to keep the VPU work small enough that it hides behind the DMA.

x viewed as (B*C, H, W); grid (B*C/8,); block (8, 256, 256) f32 in, (8, 128, 128) out; fori_loop over the 8 planes.
Rows: stride-2 ref loads give even/odd rows; the 2/4/8-row windows are maxes of those and sublane rolls (-inf masked at edges).
Columns: lane rolls build the 2/4/8-wide maxes at full width, the three pools are summed, then even columns are picked by a 0/1 selection matmul (HIGHEST precision, exact copy), times 1/3.
Outside: only reshapes.
Speed: one HBM read of x and one write of the quarter-size output; the separable max reuses the pair-max across all three pools.

Grid over batch: N//bn steps (bn=16), parallel. x reshaped (free) to (N, C, H*W); each unique limb row h is a (bn, C, W) block at last-dim block index h, so only the needed rows are read from HBM (limb rows deduplicated and weighted by count).
In kernel (f32): max over C -> (bn, W); adaptive max pool to 20 bins via lane masks + lane max; weighted mean over the 5 parts; adaptive mean pool over the 20 bins; written to a (bn, 20) output block.
Outside the kernel: only the input reshape and the final reshape to (N, 1, 20). Speed: memory-bound single pass over just the needed rows (32 MB), same traffic as XLA's fused slice.

x viewed as (B*C, H, W); grid (B*C/8,); block (8, 256, 256) f32 in, (8, 128, 128) out; fori_loop over planes.
x1: stride-2 ref loads (even/odd rows) max, lane roll max, even columns picked by a 0/1 selection matmul at HIGHEST precision (exact).
x2 (edge-pad + 2x2 s1) and x3 (3x3 s1 p1) on the 128x128 tile with rolls; out-of-range neighbors replaced by the center value (edge replication / -inf equivalent).
Outside: only reshapes. Accumulation f32; mean of the three terms in-kernel.
Speed: one HBM read and one quarter-size write; all three pools fused, intermediates never leave VMEM.
